Authors: Shah S.S.A.; Anwar H.; Alnuaimi M.A.S.; Alshehhi M.M.A.; Isa M.; Al Harthi O.J.S.; Ullah F.
Author full names: Shah, Syed Shayan Ali (60562638200); Anwar, Hafeez (57206496416); Alnuaimi, Mansour Ali Saif (60610968900); Alshehhi, Majed Mansoor Alabd (60611256200); Isa, Mohamed (59533966800); Al Harthi, Obaid Juma Selayem (60611349000); Ullah, Farman (58116209100)
Title: Beyond Labels: Contrastive Representation Learning for Scalable Image-Based Plant Disease Diagnosis
Abstract: Plant diseases are a threat worldwide, mainly in areas with limited access to expert diagnosis; however, deep learning is able to automate disease detection by methods that depend on huge datasets, which are both time consuming and costly to make. CNN's often struggle with real world image challenges such as cluttered backgrounds and noise. We propose a self supervised learning (SSL) framework for detecting plant diseases using the PlantVillage dataset. Our methods will use SimCLR-style contrastive pretraining on unlabeled images which is then followed by a fine tuning lightweight CNN (ConvNext-Tiny) with regularization techniques such as CutMix,Mixup, label smoothing which will enhance performance in low supervision scenarios. Consequently, our approach achieve an F1-score of 98.12% and 97.67% accuracy both outperforming recent CNN and vision transformers methods. By less reliance on labeled data and improving robustness to real-world conditions, this strategy provides both a scalable and practical solution for plant disease detection. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Model sangat bergantung pada dataset masif; CNN kesulitan mengolah latar belakang yang berantakan serta noise dunia nyata.

Authors: Benimam A.; Mazari A.C.; Toubal E.B.
Author full names: Benimam, Abdelmadjid (60571222100); Mazari, Ahmed Cherif (55920340700); Toubal, El bahi (57207993226)
Title: Vision Transformers vs. CNNs for Plant Disease Detection: A Transfer Learning Showdown
Abstract: The application of AI for plant disease diagnosis is an important approach toward sustainable agriculture and food security around the world. Deep learning is one of the most popular machine learning paradigms and provides compelling computer vision capabilities particularly when doing the automated analysis of leaf images for disease classification. In this work, we study the performance of Convolutional Neural Networks as well as Vision Transformers and its impact of transfer learning for the recent state-of-the-art architectures for this task. We implement four distinct models: a custom CNN, a ViT-Tiny, a fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0, and a fine-tuned ViT-Base on a curated subset of the PlantVillage dataset. Our results assert the importance of using pre-trained knowledge as fine-tuned performs best. The fine-tuned ViT-Base achieved an accuracy of 99.61% (MCC: 0.996), significantly outperforming all other architectures. The fine-tuned EfficientNet-B0 also proved highly effective with 99.16% accuracy. These models far surpassed the custom CNN (96.54%) and the ViT-Tiny (94.12%), underscoring the data requirements of transformers when trained without pretraining. Finally, this research presents a performance evaluation and provides practical guidance on the selection of paradigms between these competing architectures on AI-driven agricultural diagnostic platforms. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Model transformer sangat membutuhkan pre-training, jika tidak, kebutuhannya pada data menjadi sangat besar agar performa optimal.

Authors: Kumar S.; Kumar N.; Madhumita
Author full names: Kumar, Sujeet (57447369000); Kumar, Nitin (60570236000); Madhumita (57465051600)
Title: Real-Time Plant Disease Detection Using Vision Transformers and Lightweight Deep Learning Models
Abstract: Real-time identification of plant diseases remains essential for supporting farming production levels as well as food safety needs. The research presents an innovative technique to identify plant diseases instantly through the combination of lightweight deep learning models with Vision Transformers (MobileViT). The PlantVillage dataset serves for evaluation purposes as it contains more than 54,000 images of various crop species with 38 disease categories. MobileViT combines transformer technology to extract important features at both detailed and extensive levels thus delivering superior accuracy and speed performance when compared to CNNs. The proposed model reaches 96.3% accuracy while its precision stands at 0.94 and recall stands at 0.92 with an F1-score value of 0.93. The MobileViT model operates at 45 ms inference time with a 21.6 MB footprint which enables mobile and edge device deployment. The model operates with efficiency due to its minimal requirement of 2.5 billion FLOPs along with 0.45 GB memory footprint. MobileViT outperforms ResNet-50 and VGG16 by consuming less memory and running faster despite its superior performance results. Precision agriculture benefits from the proposed model because it delivers an effective approach for plant disease recognition which operates efficiently in environments with limited resources. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Kebutuhan deteksi real-time menggunakan perangkat mobile/edge dengan sumber daya memori dan daya komputasi yang sangat ketat/terbatas,.

Authors: Khan J.A.; Khan M.A.; Filali I.
Author full names: Khan, Junaid Ahmad (58180732700); Khan, Muhammad Asif (60131719400); Filali, Imen (57210741196)
Title: Drone-Aided Plants Health Monitoring Using Enhanced Vision Transformer
Abstract: Precision agriculture demands robust yet efficient models capable of operating on resource-constrained edge devices for real-time plant health monitoring. Existing Vision Transformer (ViT) models often underperform in data-scarce agricultural settings due to their reliance on large-scale pretraining and limited local feature extraction capabilities. In this study, we propose a enhanced lightweight ViT architecture (EViT) for edge devices used in plants disease classification. The core of our approach is a domain-optimized convolutional stem (ConvStem) architecture that replaces the standard patch embedding with a convolutional stem to enhance local feature extraction, particularly effective in data-scarce scenarios. Unlike ViT architectures, which rely on large-scale pretraining, the proposed ConvStem-ViT (i.e., EViT) achieves a notable improvement in accuracy and generalization on two benchmark datasets - PlantVillage (a widely used dataset of leaf disease images) and CCMT (a more challenging, real-world crop disease dataset). Comprehensive experiments, including ablation studies using model variant analysis, supported with attention map visualizations, confirm the superiority of the proposed model over standard ViTs and contemporary CNN-based baselines. Our EViT achieves over 94.8% accuracy on PlantVillage and 78.0% on CCMT, outperforming conventional ViTs by up to 13.6%. Computational analysis shows the model achieves these gains with minimal overhead (5.55 ms/image latency, 1.30 GFLOPs); these efficiency metrics enable real-time inference on UAVs or low-power edge devices, making the model suitable for practical drone-based scouting in agricultural fields. This work offers a viable framework for scalable, accurate, and efficient plant disease classification, making it an effective choice for resource-constrained edge devices such as drones for plant disease classification. © 2013 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: ViT tradisional berkinerja buruk saat kondisi data langka karena bergantung pada pra-pelatihan tinggi dan lemah dalam fitur lokal.

Authors: Zou L.; Yu L.; Huang X.; Li Q.; Hu L.; Li X.
Title: A Hybrid CNN-Transformer Model for Tomato Leaf Disease Classification Incorporating Gray-Aware Attention and RS-Convolutional Block Attention Mechanisms
Abstract: Accurate classification of leaf diseases is crucial for plant health and effective crop management. Existing deep learning approaches are predominantly categorized into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based and Vision Transformer (ViT)-based methods. However, inherent limitations in both approaches constrain further performance gains. CNNs excel at capturing local lesion details but struggle with long-range dependencies. In contrast, ViTs leverage self-attention to model global feature relationships but often overlook fine-grained local information. Moreover, most models rely solely on three-channel (RGB) inputs, underutilizing the texture details present in grayscale data. To address these problems, we propose a hybrid CNN-Transformer model enhanced with a novel Gray-Aware (GA) Attention Module and an improved Residual Convolutional Block Attention Module (Rs-CBAM). Specifically, the hybrid architecture effectively balances fine-grained detail preservation and global contextual understanding. GA strengthens texture representation, while Rs-CBAM further enhances attention to critical regions. Comparative experiments conducted on the PlantVillage and AI Challenger 2018 datasets demonstrate that our model outperforms existing models. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of each proposed enhancement. Overall, the proposed approach provides a promising direction for fine-grained plant disease classification, and GA shows potential in broader image processing tasks requiring enhanced texture representation. The code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/Governeson/GA-CCB. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Sharma N.; Misra A.; Tiwari R.G.
Author full names: Sharma, Nidhi (60575400500); Misra, Alok (39861843300); Tiwari, Raj Gaurang (57198002674)
Title: A Hybrid ConvNeXt-ViT Framework for Fine-Grained Grape Leaf Disease Classification
Abstract: Early and proper detection of grape leaf diseases is of great importance to maintain the health and global wine production of the vineyards. Although deep learning has been demonstrated in the context of plant disease diagnostics, the current models that use convolutional neural networks ( CNNs) tend to be less sensitive to fine-grained visual features of various pathologies since they not only focus on the local features but also on the global context features. To overcome this drawback, this research suggests an innovative hybrid architecture that makes the best of ConvNeXt, which is a contemporary CNN, and a Vision Transformer (ViT). The suggested framework utilises a pretrained ConvNeXt backbone as an effective feature extractor to learn hierarchical local features like lesions and spots. The resulting rich feature maps are tokenized and run through a Transformer encoder, which uses self-attention to learn long-range dependency and global contextual relationships across the leaf. This dual stream methodology allows our model to gain insight into the fine details of the symptoms in an integrated manner, as well as the space-based interaction of these symptoms, which is important to distinguish between two visually similar diseases, such as Esca and Leaf Blight. Applied to the Grape400 dataset, the proposed hybrid model achieves the state-of-the-art macro F1-score of 98.2, which is far above the standard CNN and pure Transformer baseline. The suggested findings indicate that the suggested ConvNeXt-ViT framework is a powerful and efficient system to address fine-grained agricultural classification problems and can be applied in the context of precision viticulture. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: CNN konvensional tidak sensitif saat berhadapan dengan perbedaan visual patologi berbutir halus (fine-grained).

Authors: Quilondrino I.C.T.; Patan G.V.; Pitao J.V.S.
Author full names: Quilondrino, Ivan Chad T. (60320517500); Patan, George V. (60320654100); Pitao, Joanna Victoria S. (58193155900)
Title: Mitigating Accuracy Loss in Plant Disease Detection: A Comparative Study of Multi-Stage Hybrid Classification Frameworks for Field Conditions
Abstract: Deep learning models for plant disease detection have achieved over 99% accuracy on lab-controlled datasets like PlantVillage. However, their performance drops significantly in real-world farm settings due to lighting variation, background noise, and subtle disease symptoms. To address this, the researchers proposed a multi-stage hybrid framework composed of three strategies—Hierarchical, Augmented, and Stacking—that integrate handcrafted texture features (GLCM + KNN) with six deep learning models: ResNet-50, EfficientNetV2, ConvNeXt, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and RegNetY-800MF. These were trained and tested on both PlantVillage and PlantDoc datasets. Among all models and strategies, ConvNeXt under the Augmented framework achieved 99.57% accuracy on PlantVillage and 91.47% on PlantDoc, significantly reducing the accuracy gap caused by domain shift. The results demonstrated that hybrid frameworks can substantially improve the generalization of plant disease detection models in complex, real-world agricultural environments. © 2025 IEICES/Kyushu University. Authors: Meghana V.; Akanksha S.; Reddy P.K.; Jabbar M.A.
Title: Potato Leaf Disease Classification Using Vision Transformers
Abstract: Deep learning has completely transformed plant disease detection by making it possible to classify leaf conditions automatically, accurately, and efficiently. CNNs have been the most common approach to this problem so far, but they can be restricted by their local feature extraction in capturing the global contextual information of an image. This current study looks into the potential of Vision Transformers (ViTs) in classifying potato leaf diseases to go beyond these limitations. ViTs use the self-attention mechanism on images by considering them as rows of fixed-size patches. This makes the model able to learn global relations throughout the whole image, thus increasing its capability to recognize the faint and scattered patterns that are symptomatic of the various diseases. Here, the ViT model is being re-trained on a multi-class classification task of potato leaf conditions. The architecture based on the transformer model enables it to place its focus on the most suitable sections of the image in a flexible manner; hence, the model is more interpretable, and robustness is increased. ViTs, which have less reliance on inductive biases as compared to CNNs, are capable of generalizing better if they are fed with enough training data. The model set a new record by achieving a test accuracy of 99.82%. These results indicate that Vision Transformers can act as an impactful aid for plant disease classification and, therefore, are the initial phase towards more reliable and extensible solutions in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Sunil C.; Gokul P.G.; Sujith G.; Paul H.; Anjali T.
Title: AgriSwin: A Swin Transformer-Based Deep Learning Approach for Crop Disease Classification
Abstract: This research introduces an advanced approach to automated crop disease detection using an Augmented Swin Transformer integrated with Mixup and CutMix augmentation techniques. The study focuses on classifying ten distinct conditions across three major crops - wheat, corn, and potatoes - using a dataset of 10,428 high-resolution images, divided into 70% training, 15% validation, and 15% testing. The dataset includes Brown Rust, Yellow Rust, and Healthy for wheat; Common Rust, Gray Leaf Spot, Northern Leaf Blight, and Healthy for corn; and Early Blight, Late Blight, and Healthy for potatoes. The proposed model enhances feature extraction through self-attention mechanisms, mitigates overfitting via Mixup and CutMix, and improves generalization across diverse agricultural conditions. Experimental results demonstrate superior classification accuracy and robustness against image variations and noise, making it a scalable solution for early disease detection in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.
Datasets: Dataset beresolusi tinggi (10.428 gambar gandum; jagung; kentang)

Authors: Nagaraj P.B.; Pulakhandam W.; Narla S.; Peddi S.; Puspitasari N.F.; Kumar L.
Author full names: Nagaraj, Pramod Begur (60136965300); Pulakhandam, Winner (59973642400); Narla, Swapna (57191571357); Peddi, Sreekar (59695638600); Puspitasari, Nila Feby (57192097100); Kumar, Lalit (60511620400)
Title: Vit-Gwo: Integrating Vision Transformer with Grey Wolf Optimizer for Robust Crop Leaf Disease Detection
Abstract: The role of detecting plant diseases is highly crucial in the preservation of crop yield and food safety. The conventional approaches to the detection of plant diseases are constrained by dependency on man, high time, and poor capacity to handle extensive use. This research proposes VIT-GWO, a hybrid approach with Vision Transformer (ViT) as a feature extractor and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) as a model optimizer to eliminate the disadvantage of previous approaches. The new method encourages the accuracy of models, generalization, and effectiveness of computing based on the deep feature learning mechanism of ViT and optimization of the capabilities of GWO. The PlantVillage data has been used for model testing, and the performance has improved phenomenally over the current models in terms of the measures such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F 1 measure. The precision rate is even higher in the New VIT-GWO model at 99.21 % when compared to the existing models. This model has outstanding scaling, robustness, and realtime usage in large agricultural environments compared to the traditional methods. Finally, VIT-GWO is a very efficient process of leaf disease detection on crops with the possibility of improvement through hyperparameter optimization, transfer learning, or effective monitoring capabilities with drone cameras or smartphones, which makes it applicable to real-world and large-scale usage in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Mehta S.; Kukreja V.
Author full names: Mehta, Shiva (58847208600); Kukreja, Vinay (49661773100)
Title: Quantum-inspired Swin U-Net transformer for soybean leaf disease detection using multi-scale cross attention fusion and spectral channel transformer blocks with explainable visualization
Abstract: Context Soybean leaf diseases pose a significant threat to global agricultural productivity, with primary detection being critical for timely interventions. The methods for disease identification support from limited datasets and generalization, especially in complex fields. Objective This study aims to develop Quantum-Spectral Multi-Task Learning Fusion Network (QSpec-MTLFuseNet), a novel multi-task hybrid architecture designed to detect, diagnose soybean leaf diseases, including lesion segmentation, disease classification and severity regression. Methodology The proposed model combines quantum token embeddings (QTE), frequency-aware attention via spectral channel transformer blocks (SCTB), and multi-scale feature fusion to capture both spatial and spectral features, demonstrating the application of artificial intelligence (AI) methods, including deep learning. A supervised contrastive pre-training phase is used to enhance class separability. The model is trained using an Auburn soybean disease image dataset (ASDID). Multi-Scale Cross Attention Fusion (MSCAF) is applied to intelligently combine features from various scales during upsampling, improving the model's segmentation and classification performance. Results QSpec-MTLFuseNet accomplishes 94.3 % accuracy, 93.8 % precision, and 94.1 % recall in disease classification, with a 0.056 Mean Squared Error (MSE) and 0.91 R2 in severity regression. The model outperforms state-of-the-art techniques, such as Shifted Window Transformer (Swin Transformer) (93.8 %) and Residual Network with 50 layers (ResNet50) (93.7 %), with a mean average precision (mAP) of 83.34 %. The F-beta score (F2 score) of 0.94 highlights the model's focus on high Recall, ensuring disease detection with minimal false negatives. Future scope It will focus on expanding the model's application to additional disease categories which detected in the field or smartphone applications. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Bahaa M.; Hesham A.; Ashraf F.; Abdel-Hamid L.

Title: A Smart AIoT-Based Mobile Application for Plant Disease Detection and Environment Management in Small-Scale Farms Using MobileViT
Abstract: Small-scale farms produce more than one-third of the world’s food supply, making them a crucial contributor to global food security. In this study, an artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) framework is introduced for smart small-scale farm management. For plant disease detection, the lightweight MobileViT model, which integrates vision transformer and convolutional modules, was utilized to efficiently capture both global and local image features. Data augmentation and transfer learning were employed to enhance the model’s overall performance. MobileViT resulted in a test accuracy of 99.5%, with per-class precision, recall, and f1-score ranging between 0.92 and 1.00 considering the benchmark Plant Village dataset (14 species–38 classes). MobileViT was shown to outperform several standard deep convolutional networks, including MobileNet, ResNet and Inception, by 2–12%. Additionally, an LLM-powered interactive chatbot was integrated to provide farmers with instant plant care suggestions. For plant environment management, the powerful, cost-effective ESP32 microcontroller was utilized as the core processing unit responsible for collecting sensor data (e.g., soil moisture), controlling actuators (e.g., water pump for irrigation), and maintaining connectivity with Google Firebase Cloud. Finally, a mobile application was developed to integrate the AI and IoT system capabilities, hence providing users with a reliable platform for smart plant disease detection and environment management. Each system component was each tested individually, before being incorporated into the mobile application and tested in real-world scenarios. The presented AIoT-based solution has the potential to enhance crop productivity within small-scale farms while promoting sustainable farming practices and efficient resource management. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: ST-IEEFO: a hybrid optimization-based swin transformer for plant disease detection
Abstract: In agriculture, identifying and diagnosing plant diseases have become a critical problem. The suggested model integrated the powerful feature extracting ability of the ST with optimization potential of the IEEFO. The study utilizes the Plant Village data and obtained better accuracy (99.8%), and recalls values (99.6%). Thus, the suggested model shows the betterment of the ST-IEEFO over other DL models. By effectively recognizing and classifying plant diseases, this approach ensures a better solution for early disease detection. Authors: Ali B.; Talib R.; Hanif M.K.; Sarwar M.U.
Title: A HYBRID DEEP LEARNING APPROACH FOR PLANT DISEASE CLASSIFICATION: INTEGRATING EFFICIENT NET AND VISION TRANSFORMERS
Abstract: The accurate classification of plant diseases is crucial for effective crop management and the advancement of sustainable agricultural practices. Early and precise detection of plant diseases is a cornerstone of precision agriculture, enabling the reduction of crop losses and the optimization of resource allocation. In recent years, deep learning models have shown exceptional performance in image-based tasks, including plant disease classification. However, the integration of advanced attention mechanisms, such as Vision Transformers, offers a promising approach for further enhancing the capabilities of these models. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning approach that combines the strengths of Efficient Net and Vision Transformers to improve the accuracy and efficiency of plant disease classification. This work focuses on using EfficientNet’s ability to extract discriminative local features from leaf images and ViT’s capacity to model long-range dependencies between image patches, thereby refining the classification process. Experiments were conducted on the augmented Plant Village dataset, comprising 61,486 images of 38 distinct plant diseases across 14 plant species. The proposed hybrid Efficient Net-ViT model achieved a classification accuracy of 93%, with precision, recall, and F1-scores of 91%, 93%, and 92%, respectively, outperforming standalone models such as Efficient Net (89% accuracy) and traditional CNNs (e.g., ResNet: 89%). Comparative analysis with other transformer variants (DeiT, SWIN) further demonstrated the robustness of the approach, with SWIN achieving the highest accuracy (94%). The integration of data augmentation techniques improved model generalizability, contributing to a 4% increase in accuracy over non-augmented training. These results present the potential of combining convolutional neural networks with attention-based mechanisms to address complex challenges in precision agriculture. © 2026, Pakistan Agricultural Scientists Forum. Authors: Zhang Q.; Zhao J.; Cai Y.-L.; Liu K.; Li Y.
Title: Toward smart agriculture: a hybrid mamba-transformer vision framework for plant disease detection
Abstract: Plant disease detection under complex field conditions remains a critical challenge for precision agriculture due to varying illumination, scale variations, subtle lesion patterns, and inter-class visual ambiguity. This study proposes MAFusionNet, a disease-aware hybrid vision framework integrating Mamba and Transformer architectures, with components explicitly designed for plant disease-specific challenges. The MAFusion Mixer operates parallel CS-Mamba and self-attention branches to simultaneously capture sequential lesion boundary evolution and global diseasecontext spatial relationships. The CS-Mamba branch employs the SS2D-LS Block with twodimensional selective scanning and Local-Selective enhancement for linear-complexity longrange modeling while preserving 2D lesion morphology. The PConv operator uses asymmetric directional kernels forming cross-shaped receptive fields to capture anisotropic disease patterns such as vein-aligned blights and directional rust streaks. We constructed PD40, a large-scale dataset with 80, 369 expert-verified annotated images across 40 disease categories spanning eight major crops, with inter-annotator agreement Cohen’s κ = 0.874. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MAFusionNet achieves 94.7% mAP50 and 81.8% mAP50:95 on PD40, surpassing 25 state-of-the-art baselines including recent hybrid Mamba-Transformer detectors (CropMamba, HybridMamba, Mamba-DETR), with comprehensive ablation studies validating each component’s non-redundant contribution. Edge deployment analysis on NVIDIA Jetson hardware demonstrates practical feasibility: the compressed MAFusionNet-T-Lite variant (8.7M parameters) achieves 89.3% mAP50 at 18.4 FPS on Jetson Nano with 8.3W power consumption. The dataset and code are available at PD40-Dataset GitHub Repository. Copyright © 2026 Zhang, Zhao, Cai, Liu and Li.

Title: Revolutionizing Guava Leaf Disease Detection-Unleashing the Power of Vision Transformers over CNNs
Abstract: Guava plant diseases present a major obstacle to agricultural yield, that leads to the emerging of accurate and efficient disease detection techniques. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have been broadly utilized for plant disease identification and classification because of its robust ability to extract features. However, Vision Transformers (ViTs) have arisen as a potential substitute, utilizing self attention mechanisms to enhance feature selection and spatial understanding. This study presents a comparative evaluation of CNN and ViT models for guava leaf disease classification using a dataset comprising 527 images across four diseases of guava namely Phytopthora, Red Rust, Scab, and Root. The models are assessed based on key performance metrics, accuracy, loss, training efficiency, and generalization capability. The findings emphasize the advantage of ViTs in capturing long-range dependencies, leading to superior classification performance. Experimental results indicate that while CNNs remain computationally efficient, ViTs achieve higher accuracy by learning intricate representations with minimal feature loss. The CNN model have shown an accuracy of 86% , whereas the ViT model achieved 93%. These results suggest that ViTs present a compelling solution for plant disease identification, particularly for datasets with complex visual patterns. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A comprehensive review on AI-based crop disease detection using leaf image classification and explainable AI
Abstract: Accurate and timely detection of crop diseases is essential for global food security and sustainable agriculture. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of recent advancements in leaf image-based crop disease detection using machine learning, deep learning (DL), convolutional neural networks, vision transformers, and emerging state-space models. Following PRISMA guidelines, the review systematically examines peer-reviewed studies (2021–2025) and evaluates datasets, model architectures, validation protocols, and deployment constraints. Unlike previous surveys, this review uniquely integrates explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) with emphasis on physiology-based interpretability and real-world field usability. Key findings reveal that while DL models achieve > 95% accuracy on controlled datasets like PlantVillage, performance degrades significantly under field conditions due to dataset bias, domain shifts, and multi-disease complexity. Critical research gaps are identified, including insufficient annotation standards, limited cross-domain validation, and computational constraints for edge deployment. Emerging directions include agriculture-specific foundation models, domain-generalizable vision systems, lightweight mobile strategies, and next-generation XAI frameworks aligned with plant physiology. By bridging technical advancements with agronomic interpretability, this work provides researchers and practitioners with a roadmap for developing trustworthy, field-deployable AI systems for sustainable crop health management. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: ViT-U-Net fusion model for accurate localization and recognition of plant leaf diseases
Abstract: Plant disease diagnosis is a critical component of precision agriculture, enabling early detection and mitigation of crop losses. With the rapid growth of deep learning, vision-based models have become an essential tool for automated plant pathology. However, many existing approaches focus solely on classification and fail to provide lesion-level localization, limiting their practical applicability in real field environments. Additionally, background noise, variable lighting, and overlapping disease regions often reduce classification reliability. This study utilizes the New Plant Diseases Dataset (Kaggle), comprising over 87,000 annotated images spanning 38 plant disease classes. The dataset offers sufficient variety for evaluating both disease recognition and lesion segmentation tasks. The proposed methodology introduces a hybrid ViT–U-Net Fusion Model, where a Vision Transformer encoder extracts global context while a U-Net decoder produces high-resolution lesion masks. A segmentation-aware classifier then uses the extracted ROI to enhance disease identification. The novelty lies in the joint segmentation–classification framework, enabling simultaneous disease localization and recognition within a unified pipeline. Performance is assessed using Accuracy, F1-score, IoU, Dice coefficient, and robustness metrics. The model achieves 99.21% classification accuracy and 93.87% IoU, outperforming baseline modules and demonstrating significant improvements validated through statistical analysis. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A Low-Resource Transformer-Based Deep Learning Framework for Precise Localization and Classification of Visible Crop Diseases
Abstract: Timely and accurate identification of crop diseases is essential for sustaining agricultural productivity and reducing economic losses, particularly in resource-constrained environments. This paper presents AgriVision Lite, a low-resource deep learning framework designed for precise localization and classification of visible crop diseases. The proposed hybrid model integrates YOLOv8-Nano for lightweight disease-region localization with DeiT-Tiny, a compact Vision Transformer, for efficient and high-fidelity classification. Using the Watermelon Disease Recognition Dataset, comprising images of Anthracnose, Mosaic Virus, Downy Mildew, and healthy samples, AgriVision Lite achieved an overall classification accuracy of 99%, outperforming conventional CNN and hybrid models. The model demonstrates robust generalization and can be extended to other crop types exhibiting similar symptoms without retraining, enabling cross-crop adaptability and few-shot learning. Its low computational cost and compatibility with embedded hardware such as Raspberry Pi make it suitable for real-time, field-deployable disease detection. The results establish AgriVision Lite as a scalable, affordable, and practical solution for advancing precision agriculture in low-resource settings. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Dynamic self-attention: A lightweight and interpretable attention module for plant disease classification
Abstract: Accurate and interpretable plant disease classification remains a key challenge in precision agriculture, where subtle visual symptoms and complex backgrounds complicate reliable detection. While deep learning has advanced performance in this domain, most existing models lack adaptability and offer limited transparency in their decision-making processes. This study proposes Dynamic Self-Attention (DSA) mechanism – a lightweight, input-adaptive module that dynamically emphasizes disease-relevant features such as lesions, edge deformations, and discolorations, while suppressing irrelevant background information. Designed for modular integration, DSA plugs seamlessly into standard convolutional backbones without requiring changes to the underlying architecture. Evaluated on a large-scale, multi-class grape leaf disease dataset comprising 9027 images, the DSA model achieved a state-of-the-art test accuracy of 99.34%, outperforming leading architectures including VGG16, DenseNet121, ResNet50, MobileNetV2, ConvNeXt, and Vision Transformers. Beyond quantitative gains, interpretability analysis using Grad-CAM and DSA attention maps revealed sharply localized focus on pathological regions, validating the model's diagnostic reliability. These results position DSA as a robust and explainable plug-and-play attention mechanism, well-suited for deployment in real-world agricultural settings, especially in environments with limited computational resources. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Comprehensive Review for Plant Disease Analysis Models Using Deep Learning Approach
Abstract: Plant disease detection and analysis are crucial for sustainable agricultural practices and food security. Deep learning approaches have emerged as a powerful solution for accurate, efficient, and scalable disease detection, surpassing traditional machine learning techniques. This comprehensive review explores the evolution of plant disease analysis models, focusing on deep learning architectures such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and Vision Transformers. Key components such as preprocessing methods—denoising, image enhancement, normalization, and segmentation—are reviewed, highlighting their role in enhancing model performance. The review also examines data diversity, feature extraction strategies, and model evaluation metrics, and identifies shortcomings such as class imbalance, scalability, and real-world deployment issues. Integration with real-time applications is considered crucial to advance precision agriculture. This review highlights the need for refining deep learning models, with multidisciplinary approaches, to ensure their effectiveness in diverse agricultural environments while addressing current limitations. Abstract: Guava fruit diseases including anthracnose and fruit fly infestation having a substantial impact on crop productivity and quality, imposing a number of problems for farmers. Title: Explainable Rice Disease Detection Via Swin Transformer and Large Language Model Powered Visual-Textual Interpretation
Abstract: Rice crop diseases pose a serious threat to global food security, particularly in regions like the Philippines, where they cause substantial yield losses. Effective disease management demands diagnostic tools that are both accurate and interpretable for non-expert users. While explainable artificial intelligence has improved transparency in crop disease detection, many existing methods remain too technical for non-expert stakeholders. This study presents a rice disease detection system that integrates image classification with natural language explanations. The system uses a Swin Transformer model to classify rice leaf images into four categories, including Rice Blast, Brown Spot, Bacterial Blight, and healthy leaves. The model’s outputs are processed through an interpretability layer that integrates Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (GradCAM) to highlight the most influential image regions and a Large Language Model (LLM) to translate these visual cues into clear, symptom-based textual descriptions together with disease management strategies. Delivered through a mobile application designed using Expo and FastAPI, the system allows users to upload images and receive real-time predictions with corresponding heatmaps and explanations. The Swin Transformer model achieved an accuracy of 96.22%, with strong precision, recall, and F1-scores across all classes, demonstrating its reliability in differentiating between visually similar diseases. This work provides a reliable and interpretable decision-support tool to enhance early disease detection, enable informed crop management, and strengthen rice production resilience within precision agriculture frameworks. © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Advanced Deep Learning with Hybrid Feature Optimization for Indoor Plant Disease Detection

Title: Hybrid Spatial-Temporal Attention Networks for Plant Disease Classification: A Benchmarking Study of Deep Learning Architectures
Abstract: The accurate plant disease identification strategies can be critical for crop productivity and food security. This paper benchmarks several deep learning architectures for plant disease classification on the PlantVillage dataset with 61,486 images and 38 disease categories. The individual models assessed include typical CNNs (VGG19, ResNet50, DenseNet121, and EfficientNetB0/B4), a tailored CNN baseline, hybrids (CNN+Attention and CNN+LSTM), a CNN-LSTM-Temporal Attention architecture, and a transformer-like MAE-ViT. ResNet50 yields the highest accuracy of 99.39%. The best result in terms of accuracy (98.88%) was achieved by the proposed CNN+Attention model based on a spatial attention module applied after the CNN feature extractor and aimed at learning to attend to relevant regions in the image for disease. The training time for this model was also reported to be the lowest at 66.1 minutes. The CNN+LSTM model, which feed spatial feature maps to a bidirectional LSTM to capture multi-region dependencies, acquires 98.59% in 68.6 minutes. The CNN-LSTM-Temporal Attention variant adds this with a temporal attention layer that runs over the full sequence of LSTM outputs, achieving 98.15% in 82.9 minutes. MAE-ViT manages 89.37% only, showing that transformer designs need big and varying datasets to stay fit against structured agricultural images. Results demonstrate that hybrid CNN architectures deliver competitive accuracy with reduced computational overhead, with CNN+Attention offering the optimum accuracy-efficiency tradeoff for real-time and on-the-edge agricultural monitoring. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: CNN-Transformer Fusion Network for Multi-Class Leaf Disease Classification
Abstract: The precise and automated identification of plant leaf diseases is essential to maintain agricultural productivity and ensure global food security. Deep learning models show potential, but individual architectures face a significant compromise: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are excellent at recognizing local disease characteristics but often overlook global context, while Vision Transformers (ViTs) are adept at modeling global interdependencies but may miss detailed local nuances. This paper introduces an innovative dual-branch hybrid architecture that combines a CNN with a Transformer to achieve effective multi-class leaf disease classification. The model utilizes a pretrained EfficientNetB3 backbone for extracting detailed local features, while parallel Transformer blocks use self-attention to capture global contextual dependencies. It was trained and assessed using a well-balanced 24-class subset of the PlantVillage data set, consisting of 24,000 images. On this split, the macro-averaged precision and F1-score both reach 0.983, indicating a high level of reliability. The network contains 16.23 million parameters in total, of which 9.00 million are trainable, providing a good compromise between predictive accuracy and computational cost. Experimental results demonstrate the stability and high performance of the proposed method, achieving a classification accuracy of 98.96%. Compared with traditional CNN architectures such as ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, GoogLeNet, InceptionV3, and VGG16, the proposed method exhibits significant improvements in both accuracy and generalisation across various augmented datasets. The findings indicate that the framework offers a feasible, reliable, and scalable solution for plant disease detection in the context of precision agriculture. © 2026 Acta Press. Title: GAN-Enhanced Multiscale Attention Vision Transformer for Robust and Interpretable Cotton Leaf Disease Diagnosis
Abstract: The timely and accurate diagnosis of cotton leaf diseases is the most important in preventing loss of crops and achieving agricultural sustainability. Nevertheless, the current deep learning methodologies for this task are heavily constrained by two issues: Scarcity of data and lack of balance between classes in field data, and the difficulty of modeling both fineresolution local lesions and a complex global disease profile. This paper presents a new GAN-Enhanced Multiscale Attention Vision Transformer model to offer a solid and explainable diagnostic system. We implement our method in two stages: a Conditional Generative Adversarial Network is trained, which can be used to generate high-fidelity, label-conditioned images of diseases, effectively balancing and augmenting the training dataset. Second, a Multiscale Attention Vision Transformer, which is based on hierarchical attention and shifted window, is trained on this improved dataset to produce features with different spatial scales in an efficient manner. The GAN-MA-ViT framework was tested on a set of 174 held-out samples and had a maximum classification accuracy of 88.51, performing better than strong CNN baselines by more than 5 points. Moreover, the attention mechanism of the model also makes it possible to generate Localization Heatmaps, which give a visual confirmation that the model is concentrating specifically on the diseased leaf areas, which increases the accuracy and practical interpretability of the model. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Mehdipour S.; Mirroshandel S.A.; Tabatabaei S.A.

Title: A novel lightweight hybrid CNN–ViT for maize leaf disease classification
Abstract: Maize is a vital global crop, but its productivity is often threatened by plant diseases, highlighting the need for precise and timely diagnostic methods. Traditional manual inspection is inefficient and prone to errors, motivating the development of automated solutions. Recent advances in computer vision and deep learning have enabled effective automated plant disease diagnosis. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) have shown promise in plant disease classification, CNNs struggle to capture global contextual information, and ViTs require large datasets and high computational resources. Inspired by mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures, we propose a lightweight hybrid model that integrates CNN and ViT components, adaptively emphasizing local or global features based on input characteristics. Evaluated on a novel, real-world dataset of full maize plant images, our approach achieves 99.90% classification accuracy, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art baselines such as MobileViT, PiT, EdgeNeXt, and DeiT. These results demonstrate that lightweight hybrid architectures can deliver high-performance disease diagnosis suitable for practical agricultural deployment. Authors: Shylaja S.; Revathi T.
Author full names: Shylaja, Santhosh (60402662700); Revathi, Thiyagarajan (56779739600)
Title: A Hybrid Convolutional and Enhanced Vision Transformer Model for Improving Turmeric Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Early plant diseases prevention in turmeric crop can enhance yield, improve food production and drive economic gains. Among other existing models, Convolutional and Vision Transformer model for Turmeric Diseases Detection (ConViT-TDD) has demonstrated superior performance in predicting turmeric plant diseases. It integrates a self-attention mechanism, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and the YOLOV3-Tiny model to enhance the models performances. ViT used to enhance YOLOV3 demands significant data and memory, requiring modifications to fit limited compute resources. Additionally, ViT is complex and lacks locality inductive bias due to non-overlapping patches, limiting cross-patch attention. This results in overly smooth attention distributions, reducing focus on important tokens. To solve this, Location Shifted Patch Generation (LSPG), Rotated Position Embedding (RPE), Local Context Attention (LCA) and Combative Loss Function (CLF) are proposed in this paper to enhance ViT performance in ConViT-TDD. In this model, ViT with a single transformer encoder block is introduced to model the images as patch sequences for capturing long-range dependencies while eliminating deep stacked encoders. By fusing Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) and a Feed-Forward Network (FFN) into single layer, the proposed model reduces computational complexity, accelerates experimentation and enables deployment on resource-constrained devices. When combined with CNN features, the proposed model supports accurate predictions. To address the limitations of non-overlapping patches in ViT, LSPG is employed for patch embedding by rotating, concatenating and splitting those images into overlapping patches for effective tokenization. RPE further refines positional embeddings by encoding relative distances between tokens derived from LSPG. LCA enhances local information by integrating spatial contextual cues through Local Coordinate Convolution (LCC) and feature refinement to capture intricate spatial dependencies. Finally, YOLOV3-Tiny is applied for turmeric plant diseases prediction. In addition, Cross-Entropy (CE) loss is utilized to improve training stability. The proposed model is termed as Convolutional and Enhanced ViT Model for Turmeric Diseases detection (ConEViT-TDD). The evaluation result indicate that the ConEViT-TDD model attains a total accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score values of 94%, 93.87%, 93.93% and 93.82%, respectively on the Mendeley turmeric plant diseases dataset outperforming YOLOv3-Tiny, YOLOv3, EfficientNetV2 and ViT-YOLOv3 baseline models. © This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. Title: Ai-Powered Multimodal Crop Disease Detection Using Deep Learning
Abstract: Plant diseases drastically cut yield and profit. Although CNNs generalize well to image-labeled leaves in the lab, performance suffers in fields because of inconsistent lighting, occlusions, distracting scene background, and overlapping symptoms due to multiple coinciding stresses. Here we introduce an AI-enabled multimodal monitoring platform that integrates leaf imagery with sensor (temperature, humidty, soil moisture, and pump/motor ON/OFF) observations and image features optionally extracted with UAVs to enhance robustness. The pipeline encompasses four model families: (i) an image-focused ResNet-50 CNN baseline; (ii) image-only transformer (ViT-B/16); (iii) late multimodal fusion of the top image features with sensor-inspired MLP; and (iv) Attentionfusion model learning image-ViT embeddings and sensor context in unison. Tested on standardized PlantVillage/PlantDoc corpora within a balanced set of 65-class corpora and an expanded 65 -class corpora set, multimodal methods reach 97-98% test accuracy with better macro-F1, especially among rare and visually ambiguous classes, outperforming image-baseline methods. Interpretabilty comes in the form of Grad-CAM maps combined with attention-rollout providing lesion location with context attribution. All artifacts (PyTorch implementation, Colab notebooks, logs, confusion matrices, checkpoints) become available for reproducibility. Our findings demonstrate multimodality fortifying field-scale disease surveillance at scale, enhancing the potential for edge deployability with farmer-accepted transparent diagnostics with context awareness. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Yiyang S.; Shuxi C.; Jianlin Q.; Wei S.; Haibo M.
Title: Research Progress on Intelligent Detection of Plant Diseases and Pests: A Bibliometric Analysis Via Bibliometrix
Abstract: This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 233 publications from 2016–2025 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, aiming to map the global research landscape of intelligent detection of plant disease and pest. Using Bibliometrix and related tools, the study examines publication trends, leading countries and institutions, collaboration networks, and thematic structures. Results show a continuous growth in research output, with China, the United States, and India emerging as major contributors, and China leading in both productivity and citation impact. Keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping reveal deep learning, convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, and object detection as central research themes, while remote sensing, drones, and smart farming represent rapidly developing fronts. Burst-term analysis further highlights lightweight models, vision transformers, and real-time detection as emerging technological directions. This study provides valuable insights into the knowledge evolution, research hotspots, and future pathways of AI-driven plant disease and pest detection. © World Scientific Publishing Company.

Title: Development of a UAV-based crop disease detection system using deep learning algorithms to enhance precision agriculture
Abstract: The shift toward precision agriculture has made it clear that there is a need for smart and automated systems that can detect crop diseases promptly and with high precision. A research project is being discussed here, which presents a comprehensive drone-based solution for detecting cotton leaf disease, combining the latest advances in deep learning with the gradual training of the machine for rapid decision-making in agriculture. In the beginning, the system implements adaptive median filtering (AMF), followed by the contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) process, which removes noise and enhances the image’s contrast. The Swin Transformer is used to identify spatial and spectral features at different levels, while the combination of ConvNeXt-V2 and the squeeze-and-excitation blocks with bidirectional long short-term memory (SE-BiLSTM) classifier refines spatial cues and learns sequential dependencies for precise disease classification. Moreover, the framework includes a Deep Q-Learning (DQL) recommendation module that supplies contextually aware crop management activities, like the optimized use of pesticides and scheduling of irrigation. The experimental results, derived from the SAR-CLD-2024 dataset, indicate a remarkable performance with an accuracy of 99.30%, thereby surpassing existing convolutional neural network (CNN)based and hybrid models in terms of precision, recall, and F1-score. The combination of deep learning with reinforcement learning in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based systems indicates a future of sustainable, adaptable, and data-driven precision agriculture. © 2026 Debbarma and Sengupta,

Authors: Kote G.B.; Patil P.R.; Bhaladhare P.R.
Author full names: Kote, Ganesh B. (59561853600); Patil, Purushottam R. (58175794700); Bhaladhare, Pawan R. (55180663900)
Title: An Ensemble Deep Learning Approach for Maize Leaf Disease Classification using CNNs and Vision Transformers
Abstract: Detecting and identifying plant diseases accurately and in time is significant to enhance crop production and food security. Maize is among the other cultivated cereal crops in the world and is prone to various leaf diseases, which seriously lower productivity unless they are detected at an early stage. Over the last several years, deep learning-based methods have shown promising results in automated classification of plant diseases; however, single-model methods in most cases cannot adequately cope with the issue of class imbalance and lack of generalization. This paper suggests an ensemble deep learning model, which can include several convolutional neural networks (CNN) and a Vision Transformer to classify maize leaf disease effectively. The suggested ensemble model is based on ResNet50, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B3 and Vision Transformer (ViT-B/16) through a weighted probability fusion approach. Here, a class-weighted loss function is used to eliminate dataset imbalance, and test-time augmentation (TTA) is used to increase the strength of prediction. A stratified split is used to run experiments on curated maize leaf disease dataset which has four classes: Blight, Common Rust, Gray Leaf Spot and Healthy leaves. The proposed ensemble model using CNN and Vision Transformer with TTA demonstrates a better performance in all evaluation indicators. It outperforms the existing techniques, with an accuracy of 98.10%, a precision of 97.83%, a recall of 97.22%, an F1-score of 97.50%, and a ROC-AUC of 99.76%. This achievement has contributed to the performance benefits through an effective combination of complementary local and global feature representation and an improved decision-level ensemble method. The architecture lowers the bias of individual models and enhances their ability to identify the difference between the various types of maize leaf diseases. This results in an effective and reliable system of maize leaf disease classification. Specifically, the ensemble has almost perfect ROC-AUC values within all the classes, whereas the minority Gray Leaf Spot category is significantly improved. Those findings show that the integration of convolutional model with transformer-based model can significantly improve discriminative ability and generalization ability in plant disease classification. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Empowering Agriculture from Pixels to Diagnosis: A Review of Computer Vision Techniques for Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: The improvement of agricultural practices relies on various elements, including plant identification, disease detection, and soil analysis. Plant diseases significantly affect agriculture, resulting in decreased production and quality of crops. The application of computer vision technology for diagnosing crop diseases plays a crucial role in modernizing agriculture and boosting field production efficiency. This technology is characterized by its noninvasive approach, rapidity, real-time capabilities, and accuracy. Deep learning (DL), a recent advancement in computer vision, has become a central focus in agricultural plant protection, offering the potential to reduce the bias associated with the manual selection of disease spot features. This article examines the methods and materials employed in the field of automated plant disease detection, including various DL models, modified CNNs, vision transformers, and the current trends in DL-based disease detection. It also emphasizes preprocessing techniques, such as image size, color annotation, feature extraction, and segmentation, as well as the evaluation of different models based on their classification and detection capabilities. Furthermore, this study bridges the gap between academic research and practical agricultural applications by providing guidance on the applicability of these models in production environments. This comprehensive review offers valuable insights into the present state and future directions of deep learning in plant disease detection, serving as an essential resource for researchers, academics, and practitioners in the field of precision agriculture. Title: Advancements in Plant Disease Classification Using Deep Learning: Trends, Hybrid Models, and Future Directions
Abstract: Agricultural sustainability plays a vital role in ensuring global food security, economic development, and environmental protection. With rapid technological advancements, smart agriculture has become a transformative domain driven by deep learning, the Internet of Things (IoT), and big data analytics. Traditional farming and classical machine learning methods often struggle to handle the complexity, variability, and scale of agricultural data, especially in dynamic field environments. In order to overcome these shortcomings, this review examines 25 recent studies that are dedicated to deep learning-based plant disease detection and crop classification. Some of the models used in the studies are convolutional neural networks (CNNs), deep neural networks (DNNs), transfer learning, attention mechanisms, lightweight models (MobileNet), and hybrid networks (CNN-SVM, Inception-Xception, and vision transformers). These methods have been implemented on crops such as rice, wheat, corn, and potato where the high accuracy has been realized in the controlled and semi-field environments. The most recent trends identified in these studies include lightweight edge-compatible models, ensemble & hybrid learning, and explainable AI for greater interpretability. However, the issues of limited dataset diversity, model generalization and IoT deployment challenges remain prevalent. Overall, this study consolidates some methodologies and findings to pave the way toward the development of scalable, interpretable and viable deep learning architectures for sustainable agriculture. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: ViT-PDD: A Multiscale-Patch-Transformer Approach for Plant- Leaves Disease Detection
Abstract: The evolution of transformer-based deep learning architectures has significantly transformed the landscape, which was designed to address limitations in Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). Unlike RNNs, transformers utilize self-attention mechanisms, allowing them to process input sequences in parallel, which significantly reduces training time and improves efficiency. The original transformer architecture work with two fundamental stages called encoder (to process input data) and decoder (to generate output). Each component is made up of multiple layers, each containing mechanisms for self-attention and feed-forward neural networks. This design enables the transformer to map complex dependencies within the processed data. Although transformers have been developed under research for Natural Language Processing (NLP) that later adapted to perform the tasks associated with several other fields of engineering. One of the popular adaptations is Vision Transformer (ViT) that has been adapted to perform image classification task. ViT has shown that transformer architectures perform better than traditional Convolutional Neural Network (CNNs). Keeping this view of importance of transformer, we have applied ViT for plant-leave disease detection on mango leaf dataset. Hence, used ViT for plant disease detection with multiscale patches reaches to 97.38% of correct detection and model throughout the paper referred as ViT-PDD. Apart from overall accuracy, we have also investigated top-5-accuracy metrics to assess well classified and worst classified class of disease in mango leaves along with other important metrics such as precision, recall, and f1-score. A performance comparison with published works illustrated on the same dataset has been included in the results section. © The Institution of Engineers (India) 2026.

Title: Lightweight Hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer Framework for Real-Time Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: The consequences of plant diseases on crops yield and the food security globally are high and hence the need to detect the disease early and with accuracy. Manual inspection methods are slow, labor intensive and also prone to error. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) are examples of deep learning approaches that can potentially be used to autonomously identify plant diseases. CNN-based models that are used in the identification of plant diseases are usually unable to provide the full context of the world. In the meantime, ViT models are effective but require large datasets, and large amounts of computation, which makes them not readily feasible in real-time implementation in mobile devices.This paper will take on the challenge by introducing a simple hybrid CNN-Vision Transformer network that is based on lightweight and effective detection of plant diseases. The architecture merges a mobile-friendly CNN backbone of local feature extraction, and a lightweight ViT of global context modeling. The system makes it more robust and allows deploying on devices in real-time, by combining preprocessing, data augmentation, and compression of the model. The proposed framework, which is based on extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, is found to be more accurate than CNN-only, ViT-only, and the existing hybrid models. This is done without the loss of low computational complexity that is compatible with mobile and edge devices. This is because the outcomes highlight the success of the lightweight design, which combines local and global attributes to offer a practical solution to the real-world agricultural implementation. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Plant Disease Detection and Diagnosis: A Comprehensive Review of Deep Learning Approaches, Multimodal Sensing Technologies, and Future Perspectives in Precision Agriculture
Abstract: Plant diseases remain a major threat to global food production, causing significant yield losses and economic impact worldwide. Early and precise disease detection is crucial for effective crop management, yet conventional diagnostic approaches are often slow, labor-intensive, and rely on specialized expertise that may not be widely accessible. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning–based image analysis, offer scalable and automated solutions for plant disease recognition. This review critically examines forty-one peer-reviewed studies published between 2008 and 2025, selected following PRISMA guidelines from major scientific databases. We summarize key methodological developments, including convolutional neural networks, vision transformers, transfer and few-shot learning, and multimodal sensing approaches, highlighting their reported performance and limitations. Although many models achieve high accuracy in controlled datasets, their effectiveness often decreases under real-field conditions due to environmental variability, limited training data, and practical deployment constraints. We discuss existing challenges and propose future research directions, emphasizing improved robustness in field environments, development of lightweight and explainable models suitable for edge deployment, and integration with precision agriculture systems. This review aims to guide the design of reliable, practical, and scalable AI-driven plant disease detection strategies. © The Korean Society of Plant Pathology.

Title: Enhanced Plant Disease Detection via Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Recognizing plant diseases is vital for productivity but remains challenging across species. This study now presents a novel ensemble-style technique which combined ResNet, Vision Transformer, Xception, and a Sequential type. It has made use of advanced data augmentation such as resizing, rescaling, thresholding, and binarization in extracting features using Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOGs). Dense layers were trained with the models achieving high detection capability across 10 plant species covering 36 disease classes. It emphasizes indicating the importance of ensemble learning in three applications as such using modernistic technologies such as drones and IoT devices to manage and analyze large-scale agricultural data; integrating disease detection with soil and weather data for optimized resource use; and real-time alerts through IoT systems for timely intervention. Title: Generative AI-Based Vision-Language Framework for Tomato Leaf Disease Identification and Context-Aware Treatment Recommendations
Abstract: This work proposes a novel Vision-Language Generative AI framework for automated plant disease detection and treatment recommendation. The proposed framework integrates a fine-tuned Swin Transformer-based vision encoder with the OpenAI GPT-OSS-120B generative language model to analyze tomato leaf images and generate transparent diagnostic outputs along with context-aware treatment suggestions. The multimodal pipeline first classifies the disease type and subsequently produces relevant textual recommendations to support informed agricultural decision-making. The model was evaluated on a five-class tomato leaf dataset comprising early blight, late blight, bacterial spot, septoria leaf spot, and healthy samples. Experimental results indicate a classification accuracy of 95.81% and semantic alignment between visual features and the generated text, highlighting the framework's potential for intelligent and interpretable plant disease management. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Optimized Vision Transformers for Superior Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Detecting plant diseases is vital for maintaining agricultural productivity and ensuring food security. Advances in computer vision, particularly with Vision Transformers (ViTs), have shown significant potential in improving the accuracy and efficiency of plant disease identification. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of various ViT parameters to determine the most effective configuration for this purpose. Using the extensive PlantVillage dataset, we systematically analyzed the effects of patch sizes, image resolutions, embedding dimensions, the number of transformer blocks (depth), the number of heads in the multi-head attention layer, and the dimension of the MLP (FeedForward) layer on model performance. We introduced saliency map visualizations to enhance interpretability and evaluate the critical regions contributing to classification decisions, ensuring the approach's transparency and robustness. Our experiments identified the optimal ViT configuration as follows: image size = 224 × 224 , patch size = 16, embedding dimension = 512, depth = 6, number of heads = 8, and MLP dimension = 1024. This configuration achieved an impressive accuracy of 99.77% on the PlantVillage dataset. In addition, we incorporated a novel cross-dataset transferability evaluation to validate the generalizability of the proposed model. Comparative analysis with traditional convolutional neural network architectures, such as VGG19 and AlexNet, revealed that our optimized ViT model not only surpasses these models in accuracy but also requires significantly fewer trainable parameters and storage space. The incorporation of a lightweight, domain-specific fine-tuning process ensures the model's adaptability to new datasets with minimal computational overhead. Our findings highlight the scalability and adaptability of ViTs, emphasizing their ability to effectively handle varying image sizes and resolutions. Moreover, our approach outperforms recent state-of-the-art methods across multiple databases, underscoring the efficacy of the chosen ViT parameters. © 2013 IEEE.

Authors: Liu W.; Zhang A.
Title: Plant Disease Detection Algorithm Based on Efficient Swin Transformer
Abstract: Plant diseases present a significant threat to global agricultural productivity, endangering both crop yields and quality. Traditional detection methods largely rely on manual inspection, a process that is not only labor-intensive and time-consuming but also subject to subjective biases and dependent on operators’ expertise. Recent advancements in Transformer-based architectures have shown substantial progress in image classification tasks, particularly excelling in global feature extraction. However, despite their strong performance, the high computational complexity and large parameter requirements of Transformer models limit their practical application in plant disease detection. To address these constraints, this study proposes an optimized Efficient Swin Transformer specifically engineered to reduce computational complexity while enhancing classification accuracy. This model is an improvement over the Swin-T architecture, incorporating two pivotal modules: the Selective Token Generator and the Feature Fusion Aggregator. The Selective Token Generator minimizes the number of tokens processed, significantly increasing computational efficiency and facilitating multi-scale feature extraction. Concurrently, the Feature Fusion Aggregator adaptively integrates static and dynamic features, thereby enhancing the model’s ability to capture complex details within intricate environmental contexts.Empirical evaluations conducted on the PlantDoc dataset demonstrate the model’s superior classification performance, achieving a precision of 80.14% and a recall of 76.27%. Compared to the standard Swin-T model, the Efficient Swin Transformer achieves approximately 20.89% reduction in parameter size while improving precision by 4.29%. This study substantiates the potential of efficient token conversion techniques within Transformer architectures, presenting an effective and accurate solution for plant disease detection in the agricultural sector. Title: An Ultra Lightweight Interpretable Convolution-Vision Transformer Fusion Model for Plant Disease Identification: ConViTX
Abstract: Plant diseases have been detrimental for the agriculture industry, as they cause substantial crop loss globally. To overcome this, IoT and AI-based smart agriculture solutions are being deployed for plant disease detection. However, a diverse range of crops and their diseases pose enormous challenges to these methods. Additionally, limited generalizability and the black-box nature of existing deep learning models, together with the scarcity of in-field datasets, are the main bottlenecks in developing efficient and acceptable solutions for large-scale applications. In the present work, a lightweight model ‘ConViTX’ is proposed for plant disease classification that demonstrates improved generalizability and explainability. The compact architecture of ConViTX uses a fusion of convolutional neural networks and vision transformers to simultaneously capture local and global features. Remarkably, ConViTX outperforms nine state-of-the-art deep learning methods on four publicly available datasets and a self-collected in-field maize dataset. Furthermore, the model demonstrates explainable prediction through Gradient Weighted Class Activation Maps and Locally Interpretable Model-Agnostic Evaluations. ConViTX attains 98.8% accuracy on the maize dataset and 61.42% on drone camera-captured raw images. With only 0.7 million parameters and 0.647 billion operations per second, the proposed model has the potential for deployment on resource-constrained precision agriculture setups. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: An enhanced vision transformer network for efficient and accurate crop disease detection
Abstract: Crop diseases cause phenomenal damage to overall foodgrain production and affect the country's food security chain. Prompt, precise and accurate detection of diseases in crops is very crucial for crop disease management. This study proposes an improved vision transformer-based (ViT) network for effective and precise detection of diseases occurring in agricultural crops. The proposed network introduces an improved transformer encoder with triplet multi-head attention (t-MHA) function, a cascading arrangement of attention units with residual connections, enabling the proposed network to progressively refine attention scores across multiple dimensions, learning more fine-grain feature representation of the images. Here, we have considered the two most important crops, viz., Rice and Apple (aka RicApp dataset), which contribute a lot to the overall GDP of this country. Images of disease-infected rice and apple crops were collected from different agricultural farms under the supervision of agricultural experts. The proposed network obtained a classification accuracy of 97.99% on unseen test data of the RicApp dataset, outperforming the standard Vision Transformer (ViT) by 2.2%. To validate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed network, thorough comparative analysis was conducted against the popular state-of-the-art CNN and ViT-based architectures. Additionally, feature visualization techniques were employed to demonstrate the explainability of the proposed network's learning capability on the images. Therefore, the proposed network offers a precise and efficient solution for automated crop disease detection, with promising applications in real-time crop monitoring and precision agriculture. © 2025

Title: Detection and monitoring for enhanced prevention of grain plant disease using classification-based deep ensemble neural networks in smart agriculture
Abstract: Plant diseases lead to productivity loss, although they may be controlled with ongoing observation. Examiners have struggled long with the challenge of accurately detecting plant diseases in grain crops, such as wheat, rice, maize, millet, and ragi. Traditional manual monitoring methods can be time-consuming and prone to errors. To address this issue, this study explores the application of deep learning techniques for automated and accurate disease identification. The proposed method begins with image pre-processing using a Hybrid Gaussian-Wiener filter to reduce noise in leaf images. Deep learning models are then implemented the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse Weighted Deep Ensemble Neural Networks (DENN) for common bacterial and fungal diseases, and the Squeeze-and-Excitation Vision Transformer (SEViT) for diseases caused by specific fungi. To improve efficiency and accuracy, transfer learning is employed. The resulting system achieves an impressive classification accuracy of 99.56%. This research demonstrates the potential of deep learning for plant disease detection, which could significantly benefit farmers and plant pathologists by enabling early disease identification and intervention. © 2025 Informa UK Limited, trading as Taylor & Francis Group.

Title: FUTURE-PROOF COFFEE PLANT DISEASE DETECTION BASED ON COUNTER-FACTUAL RECOMMENDATION WITH A HYBRID VISION TRANSFORMER AND CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK MODEL
Abstract: Coffee plantations are vulnerable to several diseases that harm roots, leaves, and cherries, jeopardizing crop productivity and farmer livelihoods. Small-scale farmers lack access to precise and accessible technologies for diagnosing and controlling these diseases. Traditional machine learning methodologies are restricted to single-disease classification and lack the intricacies of multi-disease contexts. In this work, the proposed model has a unique hybrid model that integrates vision transformer (ViT) and convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for the identification and early detection of several coffee plant diseases. The ViT module identifies global associations in plant images, while the CNN extracts intricate local characteristics, facilitating thorough disease diagnosis. Furthermore, the counterfactual recommendation system models the impacts of several treatments and preventative strategies on the original images, offering practical insights. Our model attains an accuracy of 0.9881 % on a dataset of 1056 images, surpassing current methodologies. The suggested solution is included in the Affogato app, enabling farmers to make educated, customized choices about disease control. This method not only improves disease detection but also promotes sustainable coffee-growing techniques, enhancing crop production and farmer livelihoods. © This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Non-Commercial 4.0 International license.

Title: Swin-YOLO-SAM: a hybrid Transformer-based framework integrating Swin Transformer, YOLOv12, and SAM-2.1 for automated identification and segmentation of date palm leaf diseases
Abstract: The cultivation of date palm (Phoenix dactylifera L.) is acutely impacted by numerous fungal, bacterial, and pest-related diseases that diminish yield, spoil fruit quality, and undermine long-term agricultural sustainability. The traditional methods of monitoring diseases, which rely heavily on expert knowledge, are not scalable and depend heavily on classical models that do not generalize readily to real-world conditions. Recent improvements in deep learning over the last two decades, particularly with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have led to significantly greater automation. However, CNNs still require relatively large labeled datasets and struggle with ambiguous or complex background features, small lesions, and overlapping symptoms when diagnosing plant diseases. To address these difficulties, we introduce an innovative hybrid Transformer deep learning framework based on four sophisticated modules: 1) Swin Transformer for hierarchical image classification, 2) YOLOv12 for real-time detection, 3) Grounding DINO with SAM2.1 for zero-shot segmentation, and 4) Vision Transformer (ViT) and a regression head for predicting disease severity. This collective architecture can deliver accurate detection, the most accurate segmentation, and quantification of disease severity in real-world, low-annotation-based scenarios and adverse environmental context situations. Experimental findings on a curated dataset of 13,459 palm leaf images show that the proposed model outperforms all previous CNN-based models with a classification accuracy of 98.91%, a precision of 98.85%, a recall of 96.8%, and an F1-score of 96.4%. These results represent a new standard for automated, scalable, and interpretable disease diagnosis in precision agriculture. Copyright © 2025 Alzahrani, Iqbal, Zafar and Husnain.
