Title: Evaluation of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Techniques for Plant Disease and Pest Detection
Abstract: Addressing plant diseases and pests is not just crucial; it’s a matter of utmost importance for enhancing crop production and preventing economic losses. Recent advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning have revolutionised the precision and efficiency of this process, surpassing the limitations of manual identification. This study comprehensively reviews modern computer-based techniques, including recent advances in artificial intelligence, for detecting diseases and pests through images. This paper uniquely categorises methodologies into hyperspectral imaging, non-visualisation techniques, visualisation approaches, modified deep learning architectures, and transformer models, helping researchers gain detailed, insightful understandings. The exhaustive survey of recent works and comparative studies in this domain guides researchers in selecting appropriate and advanced state-of-the-art methods for plant disease and pest detection. Additionally, this paper highlights the consistent superiority of modern AI-based approaches, which often outperform older image analysis methods in terms of speed and accuracy. Further, this survey focuses on the efficiency of vision transformers against well-known deep learning architectures like MobileNetV3, which shows that Hierarchical Vision Transformer (HvT) can achieve accuracy upwards of 99.3% in plant disease detection. The study concludes by addressing the challenges of designing the systems, proposing potential solutions, and outlining directions for future research in this field. Copyright © 2025 The Authors.

Title: Hybrid Multi-Scale Neural Network with Attention-Based Fusion for Fruit Crop Disease Identification
Abstract: Unobserved fruit crop illnesses are a major threat to agricultural productivity worldwide and frequently cause farmers to suffer large financial losses. Manual field inspection-based disease detection techniques are time-consuming, unreliable, and unsuitable for extensive monitoring. Deep learning approaches, in particular convolutional neural networks, have shown promise for automated plant disease identification, although they still face significant obstacles. These include poor generalization across complicated visual backdrops, limited resilience to different illness sizes, and high processing needs that make deployment on resource-constrained edge devices difficult. We suggest a Hybrid Multi-Scale Neural Network (HMCT-AF with GSAF) architecture for precise and effective fruit crop disease identification in order to overcome these drawbacks. In order to extract long-range dependencies, HMCT-AF with GSAF combines a Vision Transformer-based structural branch with multi-scale convolutional branches to capture both high-level contextual patterns and fine-grained local information. These disparate features are adaptively combined using a novel HMCT-AF with a GSAF module, which enhances model interpretability and classification performance. We conduct evaluations on both PlantVillage (controlled environment) and CLD (real-world in-field conditions), observing consistent performance gains that indicate strong resilience to natural lighting variations and background complexity. With an accuracy of up to 93.79%, HMCT-AF with GSAF outperforms vanilla Transformer models, EfficientNet, and traditional CNNs. These findings demonstrate how well the model captures scale-variant disease symptoms and how it may be used in real-time agricultural applications using hardware that is compatible with the edge. According to our research, HMCT-AF with GSAF presents a viable basis for intelligent, scalable plant disease monitoring systems in contemporary precision farming. © 2025 by the authors.

Title: Next-Generation Plant Management System and Disease Detection Using Advanced Deep Learning
Abstract: Plant diseases significantly impact agriculture by reducing crop yield and overall harvest efficiency. This research presents a disease detection model integrated with a self-calibrated illumination enhancement model for improving the quality of the image under the low light conditions. For detection, MobileViT model is implemented with a Flutter-based mobile application, using TensorFlow Lite for real-time inference. For treating the plants, a remedy generation system is implemented using a Sequence-to-Sequence LSTM based Text Generation model. Title: Advancing Coconut Tree Disease Detection Using Integrated CNN And Hybrid Vision Transformer
Abstract: In the agrarian societies of tropical regions, coconut plantation plays an essential role in ensuring economic stability and agricultural sustainability. One of the toughest challenges in the production of coconut trees is to detect diseases at an earlier stage and with efficiency. Advancements in Deep learning techniques have opened new avenues for efficient plant disease detection in recent years. This paper introduces a methodical strategy using a Hybrid Vision Transformer model, combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and the Vision Transformer architecture. By combining these two architectures we can leverage strengths of both architectures. A substantial amount of data is required to train any pre-existing model, highly sensitive of class imbalance and also, they are prone to overfitting. The proposed model utilizes EfficientNetB3 for feature extraction and a transformer encoder for sequence modeling. The source of the dataset is the Mendeley dataset repository and consists of 5,798 images. The are classified into five disease categories. The proposed method outperformed other pretrained and traditional models, demonstrating superior performance across all metrics and achieving better results specifically for coconut tree disease detection. The proposed model performed over 98.36% accuracy in all aspects. Overall, this study has exhibited its effectiveness in diagnosing the diseases in Coconut trees. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Enhancing Plant Health Monitoring in Precision Agriculture Through Image Segmentation and Ensemble Learning
Abstract: Plant disease detection is a crucial agricultural practice that aims to minimize crop losses and maximize farmers’ profits. However, variable weather conditions and complex field environments introduce complexity into disease images that substantially affect the precision and robustness of detection models. To overcome these challenges, we propose an approach aimed at improving the accuracy of plant disease detection through the integration of two advanced techniques from artificial intelligence and computer vision. Our study aims to employ image segmentation to extract diseased leaves and remove backgrounds containing non-essential features. These extraneous elements can disrupt the learning process of the model and hinder its ability to generalize. To enhance accuracy and performance, we employ ensemble learning techniques that combine predictions from multiple classification models. We conducted experiments using a public dataset of potato images to measure the efficacy of our suggested approach. The experimental results findings indicate that our ensemble learning model achieved a test accuracy of 98.20%, surmounting the performance of baseline models such as MobileNet, ResNet, and VGG16. Additionally, this ensemble learning model also outperformed the Vision transformers architecture trained under the same conditions. According to the findings of this investigation, we recommend the ensemble learning model (Hard Voting) as it provides the best results for plant disease detection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

Title: Vision Transformer with Explainable AI for Cross-Regional Rice Leaf Disease Detection: A Comparative Study with CNNs
Abstract: Sustainable agriculture demands accurate and interpretable tools for early plant disease detection, especially in rice a crop feeding over half of the global population. This study compares Vision Transformers (ViTs) enhanced with Explainable AI (XAI) against conventional Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for rice leaf disease classification. We introduce ViTXAI-RDD, a custom ViT model visualized via Saliency Maps, Vanilla Gradients, Integrated Gradients, and Gradient SHAP. Using real-world datasets from Bangladesh and India, ViTXAI-RDD achieved 98% accuracy in Bangladesh, outperforming CNN (89%), with Gradient SHAP providing the most precise disease localization. However, accuracy dropped to 38% on the Indian dataset, revealing domain generalization challenges. The novelty lies in integrating interpretability with transformer-based modeling across geographically diverse datasets. These findings lay the motivation for multimodal models combining image and environmental data to deliver more robust, transparent, and deployable AI solutions for precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: CLIP in the Field: A Study of Plant Disease Detection via Zero-Shot and Fine-Tuning
Abstract: Integrating computer vision into agriculture offers transformative potential for sustainable crop management, particularly in the early detection of plant diseases. Traditional deep learning models, such as Convolutional Neural Networks and Vision Transformers, have shown high accuracy in disease classification but are limited by their dependence on large labeled datasets, lack of generalization, and difficulty adapting to new tasks. This study explores the applicability of CLIP, a multimodal Vision-Language Model, for plant disease detection using zero-shot and fine-tuning strategies. We evaluate CLIP in different experimental setups. Our results highlight the strengths and limitations of CLIP capabilities in the agricultural domain and assess how prompt engineering and domain adaptation can improve performance. The findings contribute to the understanding of how foundation models can be adapted for precision agriculture, potentially reducing the reliance on chemical treatments through early, automated, and scalable disease detection. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

Title: Machine Learning-Driven Object Detection Techniques for Automated Identification and Spatial Localization of Plant Diseases
Abstract: Disease detection in plants is a key aspect of precision agriculture that facilitates early detection and effective control of plant diseases. This research proposes a better approach to plant disease classification through a hybrid framework using deep learning and machine learning algorithms. Among the classification models experimented with, the hybrid CNN + XGBoost model achieved the highest accuracy of 96.3%, outperforming EfficientNetB0 (95.7%) and Vision Transformers (94.8%). The results indicate the potency of combining deep learning feature extraction with machine learning classifiers to achieve outstanding classification performance. This is a scalable, efficient, and high-precision solution for automated plant disease detection, which serves the growth of advanced agricultural practice. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: A Review on Use of Deep Learning and Hyperspectral Data Integration for Early Stage Crop Disease Detection
Abstract: Early-stage plant disease detection is a cornerstone of precision agriculture, enabling timely interventions to minimize crop loss and enhance agricultural productivity. This review explores the integration of hyperspectral and multispectral imaging technologies with advanced deep learning models, particularly hybrid architectures combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs). These techniques offer significant improvements in disease detection accuracy, leveraging spectral and spatial features to identify subtle symptoms before they are visible to the human eye. A comprehensive analysis of 14 key studies highlights the strengths and limitations of existing methods, the datasets employed, and the performance metrics used to evaluate these models, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC. The review emphasizes the potential of hybrid models to bridge the gap between traditional imaging approaches and emerging demands for scalability, interpretability, and real-time performance in agricultural settings. Additionally, it discusses challenges such as dataset quality, computational complexity, and model generalization, providing insights into how these issues can be addressed through advancements like transfer learning and explainable AI. By synthesizing the findings, this work underscores the transformative role of hyperspectral imaging and deep learning in sustainable crop management and precision agriculture. It concludes with recommendations for future research, focusing on enhancing model robustness, expanding datasets to cover diverse species and diseases, and ensuring real-time applicability for field deployment. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Bui C.V.; Vo Q.-T.
Title: A Vision Transformer with Locality Bias for Coffee Leaf Disease Detection on Small Datasets
Abstract: Accurate identification of coffee leaf diseases is crucial for maintaining crop health and yield, yet deep learning models often struggle in agricultural settings due to limited annotated data. Vision Transformers (ViTs), though powerful on large datasets, perform poorly on small datasets due to their lack of spatial inductive bias. In this paper, we adapt a locality-biased ViT architecture-combining Shifted Patch Tokenization (SPT) and Locality Self-Attention (LSA)-to improve classification of coffee leaf diseases from a small dataset of 1,200 labeled images across five classes. Experimental results show that the enhanced ViT improves top-1 accuracy by 4.0% and top-5 accuracy by 1.7% over the baseline ViT, closely mirroring performance gains reported in previous studies. Our model also outperforms standard CNNs (e.g., ResNet18, EfficientNetB0) by up to 4.2% in F1-score, demonstrating that incorporating locality bias allows ViTs to better generalize on fine-grained disease patterns in data-constrained scenarios. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: An efficient non-parametric feature calibration method for few-shot plant disease classification
Abstract: The temporal and spatial irregularity of plant diseases results in insufficient image data for certain diseases, challenging traditional deep learning methods that rely on large amounts of manually annotated data for training. Few-shot learning has emerged as an effective solution to this problem. This paper proposes a method based on the Feature Adaptation Score (FAS) metric, which calculates the FAS for each feature layer in the Swin-TransformerV2 structure. By leveraging the strict positive correlation between FAS scores and test accuracy, we can identify the Swin-Transformer V2-F6 network structure suitable for few-shot plant disease classification without training the network. Furthermore, based on this network structure, we designed the Plant Disease Feature Calibration (PDFC) algorithm, which uses extracted features from the PlantVillage dataset to calibrate features from other datasets. Experiments demonstrate that the combination of the Swin-Transformer V2F6 network structure and the PDFC algorithm significantly improves the accuracy of few-shot plant disease classification, surpassing existing state-of-the-art models. Our research provides an efficient and accurate solution for few-shot plant disease classification, offering significant practical value. Copyright © 2025 Li, Yin, Li, Zhang and Xu.

Title: Leveraging Stable-Diffusion Generated Images to Enhance Vision Transformers for Plant Disease Classification
Abstract: Plant disease classification is a critical task in agriculture, aiding in early detection and mitigation of crop losses. In this paper, we propose a novel methodology that combines Stable-Diffusion Models with Vision Transformer (ViT) networks to improve plant disease classification. Subsequently, we utilize these generated images to pre-train a ViT model, leveraging its capacity for capturing global image features. We then fine-tune the pre-trained ViT model on three distinct downstream tasks related to identifying diseases in plants. Our experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in plant disease classification accuracy compared to conventional pre-training methods. Furthermore, all our models and synthetic dataset are public available. Overall, our findings highlight the potential of integrating Stable-Diffusion Models with ViT networks for advancing plant disease diagnosis in agricultural systems. © 2025 SPIE.

Title: Ensembling YOLO and ViT for Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: As the population of the earth grows, the demand for food grows proportionally. Early and cost-effective detection of plant diseases can result in less food loss. Title: Precision Agriculture Using Deep Learning: Integrated Detection of Chilli Plant Diseases
Abstract: Chilli is an important cash crop grown in different parts of the world due to its nutritional, economic and industrial significance. Its productivity is oftentimes however jeopardized by diseases like the anthracnose, leaf curl virus, bacterial leaf spot, Cercosporin leaf spot, and powdery mildew, which have serious impacts on reducing the yield and the quality. Traditional diagnostic techniques based on the expert eye examination are usually subjective, time-intensive and cannot be used in large scale farming. The latest developments in precision agriculture have presented deep learning as a groundbreaking technology that will help with automated disease detection and monitoring. In addition to the classic transfer learning models used in plant pathology, newer models like Vision Transformers (ViTs), Capsule Networks (CapsNets), synthetic data augmentation using Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and spatial-contextual modeling with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated great potentials towards the application of robust chilly disease detection. Furthermore, edge-based deployments of AI, multimodal approaches combining spectral and environmental data, and federated learning paradigms are provided as scalable and privacy preserving solutions for applications in the field. This review describes the practice of combining these advanced approaches, assesses their relevance, and identifies issues and opportunities of sustainable management of chilly disease in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: IGNN: An Attentional Graph-Based Approach for Vision Transformer-Empowered Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Crop diseases pose a significant threat to global agriculture, necessitating the development of accurate and efficient automated detection systems. Traditional methods, including those based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often struggle to capture the complex, long-range dependencies inherent in disease symptoms. To address this challenge, this paper introduces a novel hybrid deep learning model that integrates the strengths of a Vision Transformer (ViT) for powerful feature extraction with a Graph Neural Network (GNN) for relational learning. Our proposed architecture leverages a fine-tuned ViT to extract rich visual embeddings from leaf images, which are then used to construct a graph where nodes represent individual images and edges represent their feature similarity. An attention based GNN subsequently processes this graph to classify diseases based on both visual features and contextual relationships. Experimental results on a benchmark tomato disease dataset demonstrate the model's exceptional performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 0.99. This model's ability to effectively model global and relational information proves its superiority over conventional approaches. The findings highlight the potential of ViT-GNN hybrid architectures for robust and scalable disease diagnosis in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Chowdhury A.G.; Smith A.; Atzmueller M.
Author full names: Chowdhury, Arnab Ghosh (57329472000); Smith, Amos (60374452400); Atzmueller, Martin (10240403500)
Title: Enhancing Convolutional Block Attention with Self-Attention on Agricultural Image Classification
Abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) demonstrate significant performance on RGB images and have been applied in precision agriculture to assist in processes such as weed control, plant disease detection, and fruit quality management. The representational power of CNNs is enhanced by the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), which uses a channel and a spatial attention modules. The respective spatial inductive biases allow CNNs to learn representations with fewer parameters in several vision tasks. Moreover, selfattention based Vision Transformer (ViT) models are leveraged to learn the global representations. They are memory and compute intensive unlike CNNs. MobileViT combines the strengths of CNNs and Transformers to build ViT models for mobile vision tasks. In this paper, we propose two types of a Convolutional Block with Spatial Self-Attention Module (CBwSSAM) that harness a channel attention and a MobileViT-based spatial selfattention, respectively. The proposed modules can be integrated into any CNN architecture seamlessly. Furthermore, we leverage the lightweight BlazeFace model, which has previously been proposed for face detection tasks on mobile GPUs. We analyze an image classification model based upon the BlazeFace feature extraction network that incorporates CBwSSAM, aimed towards deployment on mobile and edge devices. Our evaluation results on three publicly available datasets demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed modules towards agricultural image classification. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Vikky; Mittal N.; Kumar S.
Title: Explainable Vision Transformer Enabled Convolutional Neural Network for Plant Disease Classification
Abstract: Plant diseases significantly have threatened the world agriculture through the decrease in food availability, economic sustainability and the survival of the farmers. The significance of timely and proper detection of plant diseases is that it helps to get them before they cause the outbreak thus curbing crop losses. Common methods of detection do not usually scale all the way given that they resort more on the skills of the personnel making the analysis. Plant disease can be diagnosed by using image data, and since the development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) especially deep learning is very prompt, we focus into probing the task of detection and classification of plant leaf diseases based on Kaggle dataset, more than 53k plant leaf images, and 38 classes using deep learning techniques. Until the stage of pre-processing the image, learning model, measuring model performance, it has been taking an entire data science pipeline of the study. They employed the VIT trained and transfer learning based on the pre trained architectures like VGG19 and ResNet50. The significant issue was the imbalance and visual similarity of classes of disease during the data analysis which was mitigated by data augmentation and hyperparam optimization. VIT model produced validation accuracy of 99.7 % as opposed to VGG19 model whose accuracy was 80.56 %. The accuracy recorded on the last performance is 91.93 on the EfficientNet model. Since the solution to the identification of plant diseases turns out to be effective with preprocessing and model adoption through deep learning. It also aids to create AI driven tools of precision agriculture and demonstrates future works such as application of the models to the mobile and real time diagnostics to the farm systems. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Kumar Swamy V.; Anusha R.; Farzana Begum S.
Title: HyTran-CottonNet: A Hybrid Vision Transformer-CNN Architecture with Cross-Disease Attention for Robust Cotton Leaf Disease and Severity Classification
Abstract: Cotton crops are highly vulnerable to multiple leaf diseases, many of which exhibit cooccurring symptoms and varying severity levels-posing a significant challenge for accurate diagnosis in realworld scenarios. Existing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN)- or transformer-based models often fail to effectively capture both local lesion patterns and global leaf-level context, and typically overlook severity estimation. To address these limitations, we propose HyTran-CottonNeta pioneering hybrid deep learning framework that combines EfficientNet-B0 for finegrained local feature extraction and ViT-base for global context modeling. These attributes are combined by a Cross-Disease Attention Block (CDAB) and further refined using a Severity Awareness Module (SAM) to enable joint disease classification and severity grading. The model is trained with a... multi-task learning approach with a λ-weighted loss to balance both objectives. Evaluated on a curated dataset of 3,600 images spanning six classes-Aphids, Army Worm, Bacterial Blight, Healthy, Powdery Mildew, and Target Spot-HyTran-CottonNet achieves 99% accuracy in both disease and severity classification, with perfect perclass AUC scores and minimal misclassification. Ablation studies demonstrate the value of hybridization and attention, outperforming CNN-only and ViT-only baselines. The results highlight HyTran-CottonNet as a highly accurate and interpretable model suitable for real-time cotton disease monitoring and decision support in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: A HYBRID VGGNET–VISION TRANSFORMER APPROACH FOR LEAF DISEASE CLASSIFICATION USING PGGAN-AUGMENTATION
Abstract: Plant diseases represent a significant issue to agriculture field globally, causing substantial reductions in crop yield and considerable economic losses. Automated plant disease detection from leaf images has gained momentum with advances in deep learning, yet its effectiveness is often hindered by limited and imbalanced datasets. This work presents a hybrid deep learning framework as the integration of the Visual Geometry Group (VGG16) convolutional network with a Vision Transformer (ViT) to capture both local texture information and global contextual dependencies. To overcome data scarcity, Progressive Growing of GANs (PGGAN) is employed to synthesize realistic plant leaf images for augmentation. Experimental results on tomato and potato disease datasets demonstrate that the proposed VGG16–ViT model achieves superior performance compared to conventional CNN and transformer-based baselines. Without augmentation, the hybrid model attains 92.67% accuracy on the tomato dataset and potato dataset. With PGGAN augmentation, classification accuracy improves substantially to 98.49%. These findings highlight the potential of combining hybrid deep learning architectures with GAN-based data augmentation to enhance accuracy, robustness, and generalization in automated plant disease diagnosis. © 2025, Diogenes Co. Title: A Novel Vision Transformer Approach with Adaptive Segmentation for Early Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Early and accurate detection of plant diseases is of prime importance for farming and food production. Conventional methods in detecting plant diseases usually cannot guarantee speed and often tend to be inaccurate. In addition, the recent AI models that have advanced the situation are still unsure of where precisely to target the ailing parts of the plant, reducing their precision. This project introduces a novel AI model called Adaptive Vision Transformer or AViT for short, developed to solve this problem. AViT also implements a new algorithm called Adaptive Attention Segmentation (AAS) that helps the model focus more on the diseased spot and suppress noise in the background. Therefore, AViT can further refine its performances for disease recognition and classification. Preliminary tests proved that AViT is profoundly better than the traditional method in identifying plant diseases, ensuring that improvements in plant health monitoring will be made. This research introduced more precise AI solutions within the agricultural industry so that farmers may be better equipped to diagnose plant diseases earlier with higher accuracy. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Dhakyanaikabdel K.; Anandababu J.
Author full names: Dhakyanaikabdel, Kotranaik (60536188300); Anandababu, J. (60535811500)
Title: A Hybrid CNN–Vision Transformer Framework for Optimized Leaf Disease Detection Using Feature Fusion and Transfer Learning
Abstract: Plant disease of leaves drastically affects the yields of crops, which is a threat to food security and financial sustainability of agricultural enterprises. Early identification of diseases with accuracy is vital for precision farming, i.e., smart farming. Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) classifiers, being conventional, have already been employed for the sake of disease classification. These Machine Learning (ML) classifiers, nevertheless, are liable to be biased towards handcrafted features, sensitivity to lighting, background, and severity of disease, leading to lower accuracy and generalizability. To address these limitations, this study suggests a new hybrid deep learning architecture called Convolutional Neural Network – Vision Transformer (CNN-ViT), which unifies the spatial feature extraction of CNN with the Vision Transformers' global attention mechanism. As a result, the combined model can automatically capture hierarchical features and long-distance relationships from enhanced and preprocessed images of leaves, facilitating effective multiclass classification. Evaluation of the model is conducted based on a publicly available plant disease dataset, resulting in better performance than conventional ML techniques and individual deep learning models. The hybrid CNN–ViT framework combines the CNN’s ability to extract spatial features with the Vision Transformer’s long-range attention. We evaluated the framework on the Plant Village (banana subset) with a batch size of 32, learning rate 0.001, and 50 epochs. The hybrid framework was 8.4 % more accurate than comparable baseline CNN and 7.1 % and 6.5 % more precice and recall compared with the comparable baseline ViT, respectively. The model, while showing increased robustness, requires increased computational complexity and inference latency and is therefore key to scaleable real-time deployment. This combined methodology presents a scalable and efficient solution for real-time monitoring of leaf diseases and contributes towards the development of AI-powered smart agriculture. © 2025, Department of Agribusiness, Universitas Muhammadiyah Yogyakarta. All rights reserved.

Title: GMaxViT: Gabor Multi-axis Vision Transformer for Tomato Disease Identification
Abstract: Plant disease detection is one of the most important topics of precision agriculture that aims to protect and boost crop yields. Commonly, intelligent systems based on Convolutional Neural Networks are employed to identify various plant diseases by analyzing images of leaves. For more complex scenarios, such as images captured directly from agricultural fields, advanced deep learning models incorporating attention mechanisms and bottleneck layers are preferred. In this context, the MaxViT model has demonstrated exceptional performance, thanks to its specialized architecture that integrates Mobile Inverted Bottleneck Convolutions along with both block and grid attention mechanisms. Presently, we propose an enhanced version of the MaxViT by incorporating texture features. Specifically, we apply a Gabor filter to the output of the stem convolution block, and the averaged filtered image is then added to the input of the MaxViT block in order to introduce additional texture information. We evaluate our approach on two benchmark datasets of tomato leaf diseases. The first, PlantVillage, contains laboratory-prepared leaf images, while the second, extracted from the PlantWild dataset, includes images captured in wild. Experimental results show that the proposed Gabor-MaxViT model achieves up to a 2.98% performance improvement over the basic MaxViT and surpasses several state-of-the-art systems. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Karthick J.; Reddy M.B.; Karthick L.C.; Eswari A.
Title: Farm Sage Multilingual Agricultural Q&A Assistant and Plant Leaf Disease Detection
Abstract: This work proposes an AI-powered agricultural decision-support system to overcome the limitations of traditional advisory mechanisms that often fail either in their diagnostic acumen or contextual awareness. In this respect, the proposed approach integrates a hybrid convolutional neural network-Swin Transformer architecture for plant disease detection with a multilingual conversational module powered by Google Gemini. The hybrid visual framework merges convolutional feature extraction with shifted-window selfattention, thus accurately identifying subtle and globally distributed disease patterns within natural farm images. The conversational module interprets farmer queries across regional languages, assuring reliable intent understanding and domainspecific response generation. Real-time meteorological data from the OpenWeatherMap API have been integrated to align diagnoses with localized environmental risks, rendering more actionable recommendations. The empirical investigation shows that the system has outperformed traditional CNN-based architectures on accuracy, precision, recall, and robustness metrics. Collectively, the framework offers a scalable, contextaware, and multilingual solution for enhanced crop health management under precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: FLitViT: Vision Transformers-Based Federated Learning Approach for Plant Disease Classification
Abstract: Plant diseases cause significant global crop losses affecting up to 33% annually, threatening food security. Despite advances in AI-based diagnosis, real-world deployment remains constrained by data privacy, limited edge computing, and lack of auditability. To surmount these limitations, we present FLitViT, a federated learning framework for privacy-preserving plant disease classification on low-cost agricultural edge devices. FLitViT integrates a compact MobileViT-XXS(extra-extra-small) model with quantization-aware training and intelligent client coordination for efficient edge deployment. A Temporal Checkpoint Manifold (TCM) module ensures auditability and system recovery through round-wise checkpoints. In addition, realtime client monitoring and adaptive timeout extensions help manage connectivity variability in rural environments. Experiments show that FLitViT achieves 97.8% test accuracy in three communication rounds with minimal accuracy loss in controlled scenarios. This enables cost-effective, auditable, and scalable agricultural AI, marking a practical step toward secure, decentralized smart agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: A Comprehensive Analysis of Leaf Disease Classification: Revolutionizing Detection with Vision Transformer
Abstract: Leaf diseases present a significant threat to agricultural productivity and crop quality, necessitating swift and precise identification methods to mitigate their detrimental effects and avert economic loss. Conventional diagnostic approaches reliant on manual visual examination are inefficient and susceptible to inaccuracies. Conventional deep learning architectures often struggle with a limited receptive field, a focus on local textures over global structures, and difficulties in recognizing long-range dependencies, hindering their effectiveness in detecting complex disease patterns on leaves. Considering these challenges, we proposed a plant disease classification system that leverages the pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT), a cutting-edge deep learning architecture renowned for its proficiency in visual data analysis. By successfully capturing long-range dependencies and improving feature representation, the ViT overcomes the drawbacks of conventional models improving leaf disease classification accuracy and robustness. Our methodology encompasses the preprocessing of leaf imagery through resizing, augmentation, and normalization techniques to enhance the input quality. The ViT model employs a patch-based segmentation approach and utilizes self-attention mechanisms to capture both localized and global image features effectively. Using the Major Plant Disease Detection Dataset from Kaggle, our proposed ViT model achieved a test accuracy of 98.14%. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: AgriRakshak: Crop Disease Diagnosis using Deep Learning and Vision Transformers
Abstract: A major part of the Indian economy is contributed by Agriculture. This sector provides livelihood to nearly 40% of the Indian population. The end result of this research is to build a crop disease detection system to prevent financial and resource loss that the agriculture industry endures. Advancements in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have enabled the development of detection and prevention strategies for identifying diseases in agriculture. A dataset of Potato, Apple, Rose, and Cotton is used to investigate this study. This study uses the knowledge of CNN and Vision transformer (ViT) along with feature selections that remove noisy and irrelevant data. We have used major feature selection techniques named Excess Green Index (ExG), Excess Red (ExR), and Principal Component Analysis (PCA). This multimodel gives an accuracy of 98%. It gives an average precision, recall and F1 score of 0.95. The developed model can be helpful to prevent crop diseases and save the cost of damage control. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: AgriFusionNet: A Hybrid Deep Learning and IoT Framework for Unified Crop Yield Forecasting and Disease Detection
Abstract: Global food security is largely dependent on agriculture, and modern farming systems depend on precise crop yield forecasting and plant disease detection to be durable, lucrative, and environmentally friendly. Precision agriculture has been transformed by the quick developments in machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), the Internet of Things (IoT), and remote sensing (RS). These developments allow farmers and policymakers to make well-informed, data-driven decisions. In order to maximize output, minimize losses, and lessen environmental effects, this review summarizes state-of-the-art research that combines sensing technologies, spectral imaging, and intelligent algorithms. Neural networks, ensemble models, and hybrid frameworks like MARS-ANN and MARS-SVR consistently outperform conventional statistical methods in yield forecasting, according to studies conducted in a variety of regions, including Kazakhstan, Nigeria, and multi-country evaluations. More advanced methods, like MHRA-MS-3D-ResNet-BiLSTM and LSTM-based models, use data fusion from various sources and model explainability to find spatio temporal dependencies, identify crop-specific traits, and show important growth stages. In the same way, deep learning and computer vision models like ResNet-50, Multi-ViT, and MaizeNet are significantly more precise than classical ML algorithms when it comes to detecting plant diseases. They get 98-99% of the time right. Furthermore, the combination of AI-IoT systems and multimodal data from UAVs, satellites, and ground sensors shows a lot of opportunities for automated, scalable, and real-time uses in agriculture. Even with these successes, there are still problems to solve, such as the lack of large, high-quality labeled datasets, the reality that models fail to perform well across different crop types and regions, and the need for better interpretability to encourage real-world farming. The findings collectively underscore the transformative impact of AI-driven frameworks in precision agriculture, providing robust decision-support systems that can enhance yield prediction, facilitate early and reliable disease detection, improve crop management, and promote sustainable farming practices worldwide. The findings together underscore the transformative impact of AI-driven frameworks in precision agriculture, providing robust decision-support systems that can enhance yield prediction, facilitate early and accurate disease detection, optimize crop management, and advocate for sustainable farming practices worldwide. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Leveraging Vision Transformers and Multi-Head Attention for Robust Rice Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: The pathogen of the disease which causes rice blast is Magnaporthe oryzae, is one of the many diseases that rice is extremely vulnerable to. For plant diseases to be successfully managed and production loss to be avoided, early and accurate detection is crucial. The current work proposes a unique method for diagnosing diseases of rice plants by using $A$ Vision Transformer (ViT) with Multi-Head Attention (MHA) mechanism is used to extract both global and local features of rice plant images, which provide more powerful and flexible representations than the classic Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). With the incorporation of the MHA mechanism, the model boosts the ability to focus on crucial symptoms of diseases even in images with heterogeneous conditions, such as illumination and orientation. The model is used on a rice plant image data set and obtains substantial advances in classification accuracy with 98.50, strength over current methods. The experiments prove the viability of ViTs and MHA to speed up the automation of the plant disease detection process with widespread consequences on the sustainability of agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: BotonyBuddy: AI-Enabled Precision Plant Nursery Management for Multicrop Disease Classification and Phenology-Aware Age Estimation
Abstract: Plant nurseries face a critical challenge, as manual inspection of plant health and growth is labour-intensive, inconsistent, and unable to scale with rising demand. Early disease detection and accurate age estimation are crucial for nursery quality assurance; however, traditional methods remain subjective and prone to error. To address this gap, this paper presents BotonyBuddy. Smart plant nurseries can automatically benefit from AI to monitor plant health and growth. This AI-driven smart nursery management system unifies disease diagnosis and age prediction for four tropical crops (Mango, Bell Pepper, Durian, and Anthurium) using real nursery and greenhouse imagery. The system leverages deep learning (DL) models (VGG19, ResNet50, EfficientNet-B7, and DeiT Vision Transformer) for leaf disease classification on ∼ 7,500 images and integrates a vision-based age estimation pipeline trained on ∼ 1,200 labelled samples. Two modelling strategies are explored: (i) Direct age regression/classification with Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and transfer learning, and (ii) an object-detection approach (YOLOv8) to count leaves and branches as inputs to an age prediction model. EfficientNet-B7 achieved the highest disease classification accuracies, 95.08% (Bell Pepper), 95.94% (Durian), 94.36% (Mango), and 92.02% (Anthurium), with DeiT close behind ( ∼ 89.8 - 93.7 %), while ResNet50/VGG19 performed between ∼ 85-92 %. For age estimation, the hybrid CNN and leaf-count approach achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 10 - 15 days for young plants and 12.5 days overall, with 88 % classification accuracy across age groups, with per-crop MAE of ∼ 4 days (Bell Pepper), ∼ 18 days (Mango), ∼ 21-22 days (Durian), and ∼ 15-16 days (Anthurium). A prototype web system enables QR-code-based plant identification, customer photo uploads, and personalized care recommendations. Results confirm that BotonyBuddy delivers reliable, real-time insights into plant health and growth, offering a scalable, AI-driven plant nursery tool for precision and smart agriculture. Future directions include expanding disease coverage, adopting multi-view imaging, and incorporating IoT data for higher-fidelity predictions. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Hybrid EfficientVit Model for Plant Disease Classification Using Leaf Images
Abstract: Plant diseases represent a persistent challenge to global food security, causing substantial crop losses each year. While traditional machine learning approaches have shown promise in automated disease detection, they often struggle with computational efficiency and capturing complex disease patterns. In this work, we introduce EfficientViT, a next-generation vision transformer specifically designed for agricultural applications. Our approach combines the global reasoning capabilities of transformers with computational efficiency through a novel cascaded multi-scale attention mechanism. We demonstrate that this architecture not only achieves superior accuracy in classifying diseases across multiple plant species but does so with significantly lower computational demands. The model's lightweight design makes it particularly suitable for deployment in resourceconstrained agricultural settings, potentially enabling real-time disease monitoring systems that could revolutionize crop management practices. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Transfer Learning-Based Hybrid CNN-ViT Approach for Phytophthora Blight Detection in Papaya Fruits
Abstract: Papaya (Carica papaya) is a commercially significant tropical fruit crop, yet its production is severely threatened by Phytophthora blight, a disease capable of causing up to 60-80% yield loss in severe outbreaks. Early and accurate detection is critical for preventing large-scale economic losses, particularly in regions where smallholder farmers dominate cultivation. Existing detection methods rely heavily on manual visual inspection, which is time-consuming, error-prone, and often ineffective in early infection stages. Recent machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches, including conventional CNN architectures, have demonstrated potential in plant disease detection; however, most are focused on leaf-based datasets, are computationally intensive, or require costly sensing devices such as hyperspectral cameras, limiting their applicability in resource-constrained environments. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a Transfer Learning-based Hybrid Convolutional Neural Network-Vision Transformer (CNN-ViT) model, which leverages CNN's local feature extraction capability and ViT's global context learning. Pretrained MobileNetV3 weights are utilized to enhance feature representation from limited papaya fruit datasets, combined with data augmentation and color normalization to improve robustness under variable field conditions. Experimental evaluation on a curated dataset of healthy and diseased papaya fruit images shows that the proposed model achieves 97.8% accuracy, outperforming baseline CNN and ViT models in both precision and recall. This approach demonstrates potential for real-time, cost-effective deployment in mobile or IoT-based plant disease monitoring systems. © 2025 IEEE.

Title: Towards Transparent Plant Disease Detection: Applying XAI to Deep Learning Models in Precision Agriculture
Abstract: Plant disease detection is a critical part of ensuring healthy crops and maintaining high yields. Traditionally, this has relied on manual inspections, which are time-consuming and can be prone to errors. However, with the rise of machine learning and deep learning technologies, we now have the opportunity to automate this process, making it faster and more accurate. Despite their impressive performance, these models are often seen as 'black boxes,' where the decision-making process is unclear, which makes it difficult for farmers and agronomists to trust them fully. We address this issue by introducing LIME, Captum, and Global Surrogate, methods that help make deep learning models more understandable. We tested several models, including VGG11, VGG16, ViT-Base-Patch16, InceptionV3, and a Custom CNN, using a variety of plant disease images. While models like InceptionV3 performed the best in terms of accuracy, the Custom CNN was able to match its performance while being more efficient in terms of computation. By visualizing which parts of the plant images were most important in making a diagnosis, we made the process much clearer and easier to understand. This study shows that not only can AI-driven tools be accurate, but they can also be transparent, providing farmers with both trustworthy predictions and a clear understanding of how those predictions are made. © 2025 IEEE.
Model Machine Learning/Deep Learning: VGG16; InceptionV3; Custom CNN; XAI; LIME; Captum; Global Surrogate
