Authors: Muchakhandi S.; Niranjan P.; Parameshachari B.D.
Author full names: Muchakhandi, Savita (59385250800); Niranjan, Prabha (57193487833); Parameshachari, B.D. (55342182200)
Title: Dilated Symmetric Skip Connection - Convolutional Neural Network with Parametric Exponential Linear Unit for Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Plant disease leads to minimize the crop yield and degrades the quality, so it is essential to detect the plant disease for effective agriculture. The limitations of Deep Learning (DL) algorithms in plant disease detection are difficulty to capturing spatial data and gradient vanishing issue which minimizes the method's performance. In this research, proposed the Dilated Symmetric Skip Connection - Convolutional Neural Network with Parametric Exponential Linear Unit (DSSC-CNN with PELU) method for detecting the plant disease. The proposed method has two phases such as the dilated convolution is used to capture the much spatial data and symmetric skip connection is used to facilitate the much gradient flow for efficient learning. Then, the PELU activation function is used to tackle the vanishing gradient issue in the training process of DSSC-CNN method. The metrics considered for evaluating the DSSC-CNN with PELU method are accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score and specificity. The DSSC-CNN with PELU method obtained 9 9. 9 7 % accuracy on Plant Village dataset and 9 8. 7 4 % accuracy on PlantDoc dataset which is efficient than Inception Convolutional Vision Transformer (ICVT). © 2024 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Kesulitan dalam menangkap data spasial dan adanya masalah gradient vanishing yang menurunkan performa.

Authors: Saleh H.; Alsamhi S.H.; Mccann M.; O'brolchain N.; Breslin J.G.
Author full names: Saleh, Hager (57218799328); Alsamhi, Saeed Hamood (56159911000); Mccann, Michael (57198244758); O'brolchain, Niall (57194851467); Breslin, John G. (7004753954)
Title: AI Meets Climate: Advanced Transformer Multimodal Model for Early and Accurate Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: The world's food security and biodiversity are seriously threatened by the rising frequency and severity of plant diseases, which are made worse by climate change. Plant diseases must be accurately and promptly detected to reduce these hazards, especially when environmental changes are likely to occur. This paper presents a unique method to enhance plant disease classification across 22 classes by integrating structured climatic data with image data. This paper provides a multimodal fusion model with improved prediction accuracy by fusing Swin Transformer models that support image data with an RNN model that promotes climatic data. Our proposed hybrid model integrates environmental parameters into the disease prediction framework, addressing the issues posed by climate change on the evolution of plant diseases. In addition, we propose a stacking transformer model that combines the advantages of the ViT and Swin Transformer as base models with a Random Forest (RF) as a meta-learner to enhance the classification of plant diseases using image data. The findings show that the multimodal and stacking transformer model works better than conventional models, attaining higher recall, accuracy, precision, and F1-score. We emphasize how crucial it is to use multimodal data integration and sophisticated hybrid models to create a reliable plant disease detection system.s that can adjust to the effects of climate change © 2024 IEEE.

Authors: Al-Obeidat N.; Li Z.
Author full names: Al-Obeidat, Naser (59898718800); Li, Zimo (59898718900)
Title: A Multimodal UAV-Based Pipeline for Precision Agriculture: Aerial Stress Detection with YOLO and High-Fidelity Disease Classification Using DeiT
Abstract: Precision agriculture requires scalable, accurate monitoring solutions to bridge the gap from macro-level field awareness down to leaf-level diagnostics. This paper presents a novel multimodal pipeline that integrates Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery with advanced deep-learning models, achieving broad-spectrum stress detection and fine-grained disease classification. A CNN initially established a foundational accuracy but struggled to capture the subtle signatures of different diseases. Switching to Vision Transformers (ViTs) improved performance, yet computational overhead and data requirements posed challenges. Later, we moved to DeiT with extensive hyperparameter tuning and data augmentations that gave an astonishing 99.45% accuracy on the multi-class plant disease dataset. To complement the close-up acumen of DeiT, we used YOLO from an aerial view to rapidly identify stressed versus healthy crop regions from real-time UAV footage. This two-tiered approach, wherein YOLO is used for aerial scanning and DeiT for leaf-level diagnoses, offers an unprecedented level of precision with scalability. Finally, complex output is translated by an LLM into farmer-friendly advisories to ensure immediate actionable insights. Our integrated framework sets a new benchmark in UAV-driven precision agriculture by balancing model sophistication, computational feasibility, and end-user interpretability. © 2025 Elsevier B.V.. All rights reserved.

Authors: Enireddy V.; Anitha J.; Mahendra N.; Kishore G.
Title: A Hybrid Residual Wide-Kernel Auto-Encoder With Vision Transformer for Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Plant disease diagnosis is an important aspect of managing and producing crops. Recent developments in deep-learning models provide robust performance in detecting plant disease with improved accuracy. Several methods have been devised to detect plant disease, but inaccurate disease detection and computational complexity still limit the performance. Hence, this work proposes a hybrid residual wide-kernel auto-encoder with a vision transformer (HRWKAE-VT) for Plant disease detection. The images are collected from the plant disease dataset, and pre-processing is employed based on resizing and augmentation. Then, the dimension of the leaf images is decreased by using the proposed residual wide-kernel convolutional auto-encoder. Subsequently, the healthy and unhealthy leaves are categorised by the proposed Vision transformer-based deep-learning (VT-DL) model. The VT-DL model contains an alternating multiple-head self-attention layer and a multiple-layer perceptron (MLP) block for extracting local and global features. The performance of the proposed work is evaluated over the existing models in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, f-measure and prediction loss. The proposed model achieves 99.89% accuracy and a specificity of 98.72% on the plant disease dataset. It is observed that the performance of the proposed model improved over the conventional approaches with reduced loss of prediction. © 2025 Wiley-VCH GmbH. Published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Limitasi pada tingginya kompleksitas komputasi serta klasifikasi inakurat pada masa pra-pemrosesan.

Authors: Upadhyay B.; Ganatra A.
Author full names: Upadhyay, Binal (60075771900); Ganatra, Amit (35100186600)
Title: Auto-Encoded Attention Artificial Protozoa Convolutional Neural Networks with Few-Shot Learning for Plant Disease Detection
Abstract: Early and precise identification of plant diseases is essential for enhancing agricultural yields and reducing plant loss. Classical diagnosis techniques are usually time-consuming, expensive, and ineffective. This research presents a new technique, the Auto-encoded Attention Artificial Protozoa Convolutional neural network with Few-Shot Learning (3APC-FSL), intended to improve plant disease detection at low training data levels and high precision. The 3APC-FSL model integrates ResNet50 as the backbone for feature extraction and combines it with a ProtoNet Vision Transformer to facilitate robust feature abstraction through attention-based embedding. An Artificial Protozoa Optimizer (APO) is employed to optimize cross-entropy loss, improve training stability, and reduce computational demand, enabling faster and more efficient processing. The interpretability analysis of the 3APC-FSL is analyzed via Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) visualizations. The proposed system demonstrates superior performance across multiple datasets, achieving 99.1% accuracy on the Plant Village dataset, 98.9% on New Plant Diseases, and 98.4% on the Plant Doc dataset. These results significantly outperform conventional methods in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. 3APC-FSL model proves effective across various datasets, achieving 99.1% accuracy on the Plant Village dataset, 98.9% on the New Plant Diseases dataset, and 98.4% on the Plant Doc dataset. These outcomes significantly surpass traditional methods in both accuracy and efficiency. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2025.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Deteksi saat jumlah data latih sangat sedikit (Few-Shot Learning) dengan tetap menekan ongkos komputasi.

Authors: Nurullah M.; Hodhod R.; Carroll H.; Zhou Y.
Title: Advancing Multi-Label Tomato Leaf Disease Identification Using Vision Transformer and EfficientNet with Explainable AI Techniques
Abstract: Plant diseases pose a significant threat to global food security, affecting crop yield, quality, and overall agricultural productivity. Traditionally, diagnosing plant diseases has relied on time-consuming visual inspections by experts, which can often lead to errors. Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Vision Transformers (ViTs), and Convolutional Neural Networks, offer a faster, automated alternative for identifying plant diseases through leaf image analysis. However, these models are often criticized for their “black box” nature, limiting trust in their predictions due to a lack of transparency. Our findings show that incorporating Explainable AI (XAI) techniques, such as Grad-CAM, Integrated Gradients, and LIME, significantly improves model interpretability, making it easier for practitioners to identify the underlying symptoms of plant diseases. This study not only contributes to the field of plant disease detection but also offers a novel perspective on improving AI transparency in real-world agricultural applications through the use of XAI techniques. With training accuracies of 100.00% for ViT, 96.88% for EfficientNetB7, 93.75% for EfficientNetB0, and 87.50% for ResNet50, and corresponding validation accuracies of 96.39% for ViT, 86.98% for EfficientNetB7, and 82.00% for EfficientNetB0, our proposed models outperform earlier research on the same dataset. This demonstrates a notable improvement in model performance while maintaining transparency and trustworthiness through interpretable and reliable decision-making. © 2025 by the authors.
Model Machine Learning/Deep Learning: EfficientNet (B0; B7); ResNet-50; CNN; LIME; Grad-CAM

Authors: Singh R.; Singh J.; Bawa S.S.; Singh J.
Author full names: Singh, Rupinder (59948788800); Singh, Jaspreet (57780930100); Bawa, Simerjeet Singh (58622984600); Singh, Jarnail (60508677100)
Title: NH-ViT: A Next-Generation Hybrid Vision Transformer for State-of-the-Art Maize Leaf Disease Classification
Abstract: Maize (corn) is a staple food in the world and its production is constantly under attack by folk diseases. These diseases must be detected correctly and early so that crops can be managed properly. Although deep learning has made a breakthrough in automated disease detection, it is being actively sought that it should achieve an increased accuracy and robustness. In this paper, a new deep learning architecture Next-Generation Hybrid Vision Transformer (NH-ViT) is presented that should become a new standard in the classification of maize leaf diseases. We also use the same publicly accessible data sources as the recent state of the art studies, assembling a complete dataset of Kaggle and Mendeley repositories that covers four classes, Healthy, Common Rust, Gray Leaf Spot, and Blight. NH-ViT architecture is the only architecture that can fuse an EfficientNetV2 backbone with a high level of efficiency in extracting local features with a lightweight Transformer encoder to capture global and long-range relationships between features. To validate the proposed approach, we implement an extensive experimental analysis, a critical ablation analysis of isolating the impact of each architectural component, a generalization analysis on an external dataset to determine its robustness in the real world, an analysis on computational efficiency, and a qualitative study applying model interpretability methods. The experimental results demonstrated that the NH-ViT model achieved an accuracy of 99.65% and an F1-score of 0.996 on our primary test set. This performance surpasses the previous state-of-the-art accuracy of 99.15% reported by Shandilya et al. on the same data sources. Furthermore, proposed model demonstrates strong generalization, outperforming the benchmark on a secondary dataset, and exhibits a favorable trade-off between accuracy and computational cost. These findings, supported by ablation analysis and interpretability visualizations, establish NH-ViT as a new, robust, and validated leading solution for automated plant disease detection. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Menuntut akurasi optimal dengan trade-off yang menguntungkan antara efisiensi komputasi dan ketahanan (robustness).

Authors: Munjal D.; Pandey M.; Singh L.
Author full names: Munjal, Deepkiran (57216434275); Pandey, Mrinal (56126895100); Singh, Laxman (21735211600)
Title: HyFPlantNet: hybrid feature-based plant disease classification network
Abstract: Plant disease affects agricultural productivity, food security, and, in turn, economic stability; thus, early-stage, accurate detection of plant diseases is necessary. This research proposes Hybrid Feature-based Plant Disease Classification Network (HyFPlantNet), a hybrid feature based deep learning framework that integrates both spatial and spectral descriptors for robust plant disease classification through visualization. The feature extraction modules include Scale Invariant Feature Transform (SiFT) for keypoints detection, Wavelet based SFTA (WSFTA) for fractal texture analysis, Gray Level Co occurrence Matrix (GLcM) for statistical texture characterization, and HSV color space analysis for color based discrimination. The resultant feature vectors are concatenated and filtered using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and finally fed into a fully connected neural network for classification. HyFPlantNet was evaluated on three benchmark datasets - PlantVillage, AI Challenger 2018 Crop Disease Detection, and Plant Pathology 2021 (cf. FGVC8) where it achieved accuracies of 96.41%, 96.41%, and 96.41%, respectively, which accounts for 0.1663% improvements from Vision Transformer on PlantVillage, 0.0952% improvements from Xception on AI Challenger, and 0.9741% from ResNet 50 on Plant Pathology 2021, serving as state of the art. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2025.

Authors: Gheorghiu A.; Tăiatu I.-M.; Cercel D.-C.; Marin I.; Pop F.
Author full names: Gheorghiu, Adrian (58827085200); Tăiatu, Iulian-Marius (58476340200); Cercel, Dumitru-Clementin (55681787600); Marin, Iuliana (56572307200); Pop, Florin (22836395600)
Title: Evaluating Data Augmentation Techniques for Coffee Leaf Disease Classification
Abstract: The detection and classification of diseases in Robusta coffee leaves are essential to ensure that plants are healthy and the crop yield is kept high. However, this job requires extensive botanical knowledge and much wasted time. Therefore, this task and others similar to it have been extensively researched subjects in image classification. Regarding leaf disease classification, most approaches have used the more popular PlantVillage dataset while completely disregarding other datasets, like the Robusta Coffee Leaf (RoCoLe) dataset. As the RoCoLe dataset is imbalanced and does not have many samples, fine-tuning of pre-trained models and multiple augmentation techniques need to be used. The current paper uses the RoCoLe dataset and approaches based on deep learning for classifying coffee leaf diseases from images, incorporating the pix2pix model for segmentation and cyclegenerative adversarial network (CycleGAN) for augmentation. Our study demonstrates the effectiveness of Transformer-based models, online augmentations, and CycleGAN augmentation in improving leaf disease classification. While synthetic data has limitations, it complements real data, enhancing model performance. These findings contribute to developing robust techniques for plant disease detection and classification. © 2024 by SCITEPRESS – Science and Technology Publications, Lda.

Authors: Kaleeswari G.; Sundarrajan R.
Author full names: Kaleeswari, G. (59546800800); Sundarrajan, R. (6507001906)
Title: A Comprehensive Survey on Phytopathogen Surveillance with Modern Artificial Intelligence Practices
Abstract: The most important aspect of modern agriculture is the detection of plant diseases with the goal of improving crop quality and output. This survey paper investigates modern approaches of deep learning algorithms, Explainable AI and Federated Learning to plant disease diagnosis. The background and broadening of plant disease detection are briefly reviewed at the outset of the study, with a focus on the importance of precise and effective identification techniques. The multivariate normal DL neural network (MNDLNN) classifier and Customized CNN are the most robust feature extraction and classification techniques among the examined technologies. Using Higher-Order Whitened Singular Value Decomposition (HOWSVD), complex data is processed in a way that highlights distinct patterns and features for easy data classification and also increases accuracy. The E-GreenNet generates disease classification features based on a MobileNetV3. The ResNet9 and Improved Vision Transformer models perform better when processing complicated visual data. Spectral Generative Adversarial Neural Network (DSGAN2) and Lite Multikernel Depthwise Convolutions architecture are suitable for real-time applications because they provide promising results with less computational overhead. These findings' implications point to a possible move toward disease detection systems that are easier to use and more effective, which would improve crop management and food security. The development of more affordable solutions for small scale farmers, the integration of Embedded systems for real-time monitoring, and the improvement of these models for increased precision are some future directions. This survey highlights the transformative potential of combining deep learning with other techniques like Federated Learning in advancing agricultural practices. © 2024 IEEE.
Model Machine Learning/Deep Learning: MNDLNN; Customized CNN; MobileNetV3; ResNet-9; DSGAN2
Tantangan/Research Gap: Kebutuhan integrasi sistem embedded yang murah, deteksi real-time, dan mudah digunakan petani.

Authors: Lakshman M.; Kumar T.B.
Author full names: Lakshman, Manikala (59670118300); Kumar, T. Bharath (57222536219)
Title: Advances in Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Plant Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Review
Abstract: Diseases affecting plants pose a substantial risk to agricultural output, notably in regions like India where farming underpins both internal food supplies and overseas commerce. Conventional strategies for spotting plant diseases depend on expert visual assessments, which are demanding in terms of time and resources, rendering them unsuitable for vast agricultural areas. Machine learning and deep learning emerge as promising tools to address these issues by automating identification processes. This comprehensive review aims to analyze and synthesize recent advances in machine learning and deep learning methodologies for automated plant disease detection, with particular focus on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs). The study examines various architectures, datasets, preprocessing techniques, and their comparative performance across different agricultural contexts. Our analysis reveals that while traditional machine learning methods achieve 90-97% accuracy in controlled environments, deep learning approaches, particularly hybrid CNN-ViT architectures, demonstrate superior performance with accuracies reaching 95-99.7% even in variable field conditions. This review identifies critical gaps in current research including computational constraints, limited dataset diversity, and field adaptability challenges, while proposing future directions toward lightweight models, multimodal data integration, and edge computing solutions for sustainable precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Limitasi komputasional, dataset yang sempit, keterbatasan adaptasi lingkungan nyata, dan integrasi data multimodal.

Authors: Pavan Kalyan G.; Chinna B.; Senthil S.; Chundi R.
Author full names: Pavan Kalyan, G. (60546857500); Chinna, Bhukya (60546536300); Senthil, S. (57192388274); Chundi, Ramesh (57221564290)
Title: Sorghum Leaf Disease Detection Using Vision Transformer
Abstract: Sorghum is a key cereal crop cultivated extensively in semi-arid regions, where food security is greatly impacted by it. However, foliar diseases frequently impair its yield and quality, necessitating prompt discovery for efficient control. This study introduces a deep learning-based framework leveraging the Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture to classify various sorghum leaf diseases directly from raw images. In contrast to conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs), ViT employs self-attention mechanisms to model long-range dependencies within image patches, enabling more robust feature learning. A publicly available sorghum leaf disease dataset was curated, preprocessed, and augmented to improve model generalization. Using the ViT-B/16 variant, The suggested model outperformed many CNN baselines with a classification accuracy of 95.4%. Performance was evaluated across all illness categories using evaluation criteria like precision, recall, and F1-score. The results demonstrate transformer-based models' promise as a scalable and practical remedy for automated plant disease identification, supporting real-time monitoring in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Bandara L.M.; Seneviratne O.; Kalupahana D.; Silva B.N.; Wijenayake U.; Wijesinghe R.E.
Author full names: Bandara, Lakshan Madhushanka (60525153900); Seneviratne, Ovini (60241862800); Kalupahana, Deshan (59302759700); Silva, Bhagya Nathali (57192304387); Wijenayake, Udaya (55547801900); Wijesinghe, Ruchire Eranga (56018152300)
Title: Comparative Analysis of Transformer and CNN Architectures for OCT-Based Detection of Circular Leaf Spot Disease in Diospyros kaki
Abstract: Circular Leaf Spot (CLS) disease caused by Mycosphaerella nawae poses a significant threat to the cultivation of Diospyros kaki (persimmon). Early and accurate identification is essential to reduce yield loss, yet conventional diagnostic methods are often invasive, subjective, or time-consuming. Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) offers a non-destructive imaging technique capable of revealing detailed leaf structures, allowing the use of deep learning models for automated disease classification. This study investigates the performance of transformer-based architectures, including ViT, Swin, CoaT, ConViT, LeViT, and MobileViT, for the classification of CLS disease OCT images. The same dataset as in previous CNN-based research was used, applying identical preprocessing techniques for fair comparison. Research was conducted using a 5-fold cross-validation, and transformer models were compared with traditional CNNs from the previous research, such as DenseNet121, VGG16, and Xception. The results show that Transformer architectures, particularly the hybrid CoaT model, achieve superior overall accuracy (87.6%) and micro-averaged AUC (0.974), surpassing the best CNN-based models. The findings highlight the strong potential of transformer architectures in the diagnosis of plant diseases using OCT, especially for early-stage detection. This research underscores the suitability of advanced vision models for high-resolution non-destructive classification tasks in agriculture. © 2026 IEEE.

Authors: Saleh H.; Mccann M.; Creaven R.; Breslin J.G.; El-Sappagh S.
Author full names: Saleh, Hager (57218799328); Mccann, Michael (57198244758); Creaven, Ross (60466122500); Breslin, John G. (7004753954); El-Sappagh, Shaker (60431764900)
Title: Hybrid CNN-Swin Framework for Detection and Classification of Potato Leaf Diseases
Abstract: Timely and accurate identification of plant diseases is essential for sustainable agricultural practices and food security. This study presents a deep learning-based diagnostic framework capable of classifying seven potato leaf conditions: healthy, early blight, late blight, brown spot, target spot, bacterial wilt, and leaf curl. Despite significant progress in plant disease detection using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), existing approaches often struggle with inter-class similarity and lack generalization across variable imaging conditions. To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid model that integrates a CNN architecture (i.e., EfficientNetB0) with the Swin Transformer, leveraging their complementary feature representations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid model outperforms individual baselines, achieving an accuracy of 91.734%, precision of 92.204%, recall of 91.734%, and F1-score of 91.71% across all seven classes. These findings highlight the model's robustness and its potential to support scalable, real-time disease monitoring in precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Nisha J.C.; Victoria K.R.R.; Rose G.L.; Navaneethan S.; Maheswari S.; Ashini K.
Title: Multi-Spectral Vision Transformers for Early Crop Disease Detection Under Natural Field Variability
Abstract: The given paper describes an integrated approach to the early detection of crop diseases in real-time through a new Multi-Spectral Vision Transformer (MSViT). The method proposed incorporates spatial, spectral and contextual information by simultaneously processing the RGB as well as the near-infrared (NIR) channels with a dual-stream transformer encoder, which trains on cross-spectral attention. Extrinsic spectral enhancement block is added to enhance the faint physical stress signals that are not easily seen in normal imagery. In order to combat field-level ailments like illumination shifts, soil background noise, leaf occlusion, and phenological variation, add an adaptive domain-aware normalization layer which dynamically adjusts the scaling of features depending on environmental metadata. This model is trained in a self-supervised spectral consistency objective to minimize the use of large annotated datasets. The experimental findings of multi-spectral field datasets show that MSViT has a higher accuracy of 96.4% in the early stage of detecting diseases and is stable under real-world scenarios. The approach provides a scalable approach that can be used in precision agriculture and automated crop health-sensing. © 2025 IEEE.
Tantangan/Research Gap: Hambatan pencahayaan lapangan, gangguan latar-tanah (noise), serta kondisi fenologis lingkungan alam sekitar.

Authors: Chettri K.; Sen B.; Yumlembam R.A.; Ghosal P.
Author full names: Chettri, Kishor (59870045300); Sen, Biswaraj (57193872725); Yumlembam, Rupert Anand (57200919011); Ghosal, Palash (57195280784)
Title: ResNet-Swin Transformer Fusion with Shifted Window Attention for Multi-Class Plant Disease Classification with Weighted Sampling
Abstract: Plant diseases pose a critical challenge to global agriculture, contributing to significant crop losses and threatening food security. Conventional disease identification methods such as manual inspections and laboratory tests are often inefficient and labor intensive, prone to misdiagnosis due to the visual similarity of symptoms between different diseases. This paper introduces a hybrid deep learning model that combines the ResNet-50 and Swin Transformer architectures to improve plant disease classification by capturing localized and global contextual features. Comprehensive augmentation approaches: rotation, flipping, color jittering, resized cropping, Gaussian blur ensure robust learning across diverse datasets. Our study includes several datasets, proving the robustness of the model across largescale datasets such as PlantVillage (99.87 %), real-time dataset such as PlantDoc (81.00 %), and as well as its flexibility in smaller, domain-specific datasets such as the Rice Leaf dataset (92.00 %) accuracy on the test set. A weighted cross-entropy loss along with a WeightedRandomSampler is used to reduce class imbalance, an Adam optimizer is used with a ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler to modify the learning rate dynamically, and early stopping is used to prevent overfitting. These components collectively enable the model to achieve state-of-the-art accuracy for multi-class plant disease classification on the PlantVillage dataset while maintaining competitive performance across other benchmark datasets, underscoring its potential as a scalable solution for precision agriculture and disease diagnostics. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Mailapur C.; Sadanala S.K.; Sudarshi M.; Sayolla S.C.; Vikruthi S.
Author full names: Mailapur, Chetana (59999300000); Sadanala, Surya Kumari (59999194400); Sudarshi, Mamatha (59999300100); Sayolla, Sai Chaithanya (59999142700); Vikruthi, SriHarsha (57216763981)
Title: Enhanced Vision Transformer with Adaptive Segmentation for Precise Plant Diseases Detection
Abstract: Early and accurate detection of plant diseases is of prime importance for agriculture and food production. Conventional methods in detecting plant diseases usually cannot guarantee speed and often tend to be inaccurate. In addition, recent AI models that have advanced the situation are still uncertain of where precisely to target the ailing parts of the plant, reducing their precision. Plant diseases threaten agricultural productivity, requiring early and accurate detection for effective management. Existing methods often lack precision in classification, localization, and segmentation. This project improves upon them using deep learning models - CNN for classification, Faster R-CNN for object detection, and U-Net for segmentation - on the PlantVillage dataset, which includes leaves, stems, and roots. this approach improves accuracy, disease localization, and segmentation compared to traditional methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of deep learning in automated plant disease diagnosis, contributing to smart agriculture and precision agriculture. © 2025 IEEE.

Authors: Latif S.; Mastoi Q.-U.-A.; Almujally N.A.; Alnazzawi N.; Hanif M.; Latif S.
Author full names: Latif, Sara (57212765468); Mastoi, Qurat-Ul-Ain (57200855422); Almujally, Nouf Abdullah (57193325656); Alnazzawi, Noha (57190124338); Hanif, Muhammad (57210377659); Latif, Shahid (57216963065)
Title: Optimizing agricultural health using a compact convolutional transformer model for plant disease detection
Abstract: Introduction: Plant diseases present a significant global challenge to agricultural productivity and food security, necessitating efficient and accurate detection methods. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) often struggle to capture long-range dependencies and global contextual information, while vision transformers (ViTs) require substantial computational resources, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained environments. Methods: This article introduces a compact convolutional transformer (CCT) model that effectively combines the local feature extraction capabilities of CNNs with the global contextual understanding of transformers. The proposed architecture employs a convolutional tokenization stage to generate semantically rich patches, followed by a lightweight transformer encoder that models complex spatial relationships essential for fine-grained disease recognition. Results: Extensive experiments on a new plant disease dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework, achieving an overall accuracy of 93.55%. The model also exhibits remarkable efficiency, with a compact size of 16.66 MB and an inference time of 0.7 ms per image, making it suitable for edge deployment. Conclusion: Experimental outcomes significantly outperform existing state-of-the-art methods, highlighting the potential of the proposed CCT-based framework for real-world, scalable plant disease diagnosis in diverse agricultural settings. © 2025 CABI International.
